item.title: Colombia le ofrece a EE.UU. sus minerales críticos: qué dicen los memorandos y qué riesgos existen
item.description: Estados Unidos y Colombia establecieron un marco de cooperación para minerales críticos y tierras raras que contempla movilizar apoyo público y privado para identificar y financiar conjuntamente proye ...
item.dc:creator: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — Colombia afronta el reto de aprovechar la cooperación con Estados Unidos en minerales críticos para avanzar en las cadenas de valor, atraer transferencia de tecnología y conocimiento y evitar quedar limitada únicamente a la exportación de materias primas, según expertos. Durante su reciente visita a Colombia, el secretario de Estado de EE.UU., Marco Rubio, y el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores colombiano, Omar Bula, suscribieron dos instrumentos de cooperación para fortalecer las cadenas de suministro de minerales críticos y tierras raras, así como avanzar en la cooperación estratégica en materia de energía nuclear civil. Vladimir Rouvinski, director del Laboratorio de Política y Relaciones Internacionales de la Universidad Icesi, señala a este medio que el acuerdo entre Colombia y Estados Unidos implica tanto oportunidades como riesgos para el país sudamericano, en el marco del nuevo acercamiento de Washington hacia el hemisferio occidental. Entre las oportunidades, destaca la posibilidad de que Colombia pase de exportar minerales a participar en una cadena de valor, lo que permitiría acceder a capital, tecnología y conocimiento que el país no necesariamente posee en todos los casos. Rouvinski también considera que el acercamiento con Estados Unidos puede fortalecer el papel de Colombia como proveedor estratégico de minerales para ese país y contribuir a formalizar actividades que actualmente están dominadas, en algunos casos, por la economía ilegal o no formalizada. Ver más: Latam pone los minerales para energías limpias, pero países ricos son los que ganan: Oxfam “Ahora bien, lo importante es tener en cuenta que Colombia tiene que saber defender sus intereses, dejando muy claro cuál es el interés del país”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea Vladimir Rouvinski. “Y aquí no se trata simplemente de ser parte de esta cadena de valor, sino de cuál puede ser la participación efectiva que tiene Colombia”. Rouvinski señala que Colombia debe considerar los impactos ambientales y los conflictos socioambientales y territoriales que pueden surgir con el desarrollo de la actividad, ya que estos factores podrían agravar los problemas asociados con la minería ilegal y la captura criminal. Otro aspecto que considera relevante es la dependencia tecnológica. Según Rouvinski, Colombia debe procurar la transferencia de tecnología y conocimiento para evitar limitarse nuevamente a la exportación de materias primas y convertirse en un socio dentro de esta nueva esfera económica. Desde una perspectiva geopolítica, Rouvinski señala que tanto China como Estados Unidos están fortaleciendo sus cadenas de suministro de minerales críticos. Por ello, considera que Colombia debe mantener claros sus intereses al profundizar su relación con Estados Unidos, sin poner en riesgo las relaciones que pueda mantener con otros potenciales socios. Ver más: Qué son y cómo invertir en minerales críticos, indispensables para la IA, la energía y la defensa El acercamiento entre Colombia y EE.UU. se produce en un momento en el que las principales potencias mundiales buscan asegurar el suministro de minerales críticos para industrias estratégicas como la IA. La Agencia Internacional de Energía señala que el fuerte crecimiento de la demanda de estos materiales ha elevado su valor estratégico y llevado a los gobiernos a priorizar cadenas de suministro más “seguras y resilientes”. “Colombia cuenta con un marco jurídico sólido para el desarrollo de los minerales estratégicos. Básicamente se ha fomentado la metodología de las rondas de selección objetiva como mecanismo de contratación, pero también no se descarta que se modifique el marco jurídico y regulatorio para atraer inversión en materia de exploración”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea Milton Montoya, analista del sector y counsel del bufete de abogados Holland & Knight. El acuerdo con EE.UU. no implica la entrega de áreas mineras, la asignación de contratos ni compromisos de recursos por parte de Colombia, dijo Montoya, quien lo definió como una declaración de intenciones para establecer áreas de cooperación entre ambos países. “Se busca fomentar la exploración, es decir, el conocimiento del subsuelo y, a partir de ahí, en las áreas donde se identifiquen recursos, avanzar en su exploración y en el desarrollo industrial de los minerales críticos”, anotó el abogado Montoya. El Departamento de Estado estadounidense señaló que el memorando de entendimiento apunta a la simplificación de los trámites de concesión de permisos, a mecanismos de fijación de precios que protejan el mercado (como los precios mínimos), a herramientas de evaluación de la seguridad nacional para la venta de activos de minerales críticos, a la inversión en tecnología de reciclaje de minerales y a la cooperación en materia de cartografía geológica. “Establece un marco entre Estados Unidos y Colombia para garantizar cadenas de suministro resilientes, diversificadas y justas de minerales críticos y tierras raras, comprometiendo a ambos gobiernos a movilizar el apoyo del sector público y privado, mediante garantías, préstamos, capital, acuerdos de compra, seguros o medidas de facilitación normativa, con el fin de identificar y financiar conjuntamente proyectos de extracción y procesamiento en un plazo de seis meses a partir de la firma”, dijo en un comunicado. A propósito de la suscripción de los instrumentos de cooperación con EE.UU., el Instituto de Ciencia Política Hernán Echavarría Olózaga (ICP) señaló en un comunicado que el memorando sobre minerales críticos abre una oportunidad para atraer inversión y desarrollar proyectos. “El reto para Colombia es crear las condiciones para que esa inversión se convierta en producción, valor agregado y una mayor participación en las cadenas globales de valor”, explicó en un comunicado el ICP. ICP propone que el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2026-2030 podría incluir reformas para dar mayor previsibilidad a las reglas del sector y facilitar proyectos mineros de largo plazo. Entre las propuestas están crear un Estatuto Minero y Fiscal para Minerales Estratégicos, establecer mecanismos de estabilidad jurídica por al menos 10 años y revisar los incentivos fiscales para proyectos de gran escala. Ver más: Por qué América Latina gana peso en la estrategia de Europa de minerales críticos y la transición verde A pesar de la oportunidad, Colombia necesita avanzar en conocimiento geológico, exploración, estabilidad jurídica y eficiencia en los trámites ambientales y de consulta previa para convertir su potencial en minerales críticos en nuevos proyectos de inversión, tras la firma de un memorando de entendimiento con Estados Unidos en esta materia. “Sin lugar a dudas, uno de los principales aspectos que tiene Colombia pendiente por desarrollar es su potencial minero. Pero primero es fundamental el conocimiento geológico y en segundo lugar el fomento de la exploración”, manifestó Milton Montoya, de Holland & Knight. Ver más: Citi revela los minerales críticos que generarían riqueza en América Latina y los países prometedores Desde el punto de vista de la política pública y del marco jurídico, Montoya señala que se necesitan cuatro elementos para aprovechar el potencial de los minerales críticos: estabilidad jurídica; desmontar algunas de las trabas derivadas de figuras ambientales que limitan el desarrollo de la actividad minera en los territorios; optimizar y hacer más eficientes los procesos de consulta previa; y hacer lo mismo con los procesos de licenciamiento ambiental. Lina Uribe, socia de Corporativo y M&A en el bufete Pérez-Llorca Colombia, expone que el borrador del CONPES de Política Nacional de Minerales Estratégicos y Críticos, publicado en agosto de 2026, identifica como principal obstáculo “la baja capacidad intersectorial para gestionar de manera integral los minerales estratégicos y críticos”. Considera que esta es una limitación que frena la transformación productiva y el cierre de brechas territoriales. “Pero el problema va más allá de un solo sector: según el Índice de Complejidad Empresarial Global de TMF , Colombia ocupa el sexto puesto mundial entre los países más complejos para hacer negocios, debido a las acciones discrecionales de la autoridad fiscal, los cambios constantes en los requisitos regulatorios y las expectativas poco claras en materia de cumplimiento normativo”, anotó la abogada. Asimismo, expresó que los procesos de consulta previa con comunidades étnicas son otro de los factores que más incertidumbre generan, tanto para los inversionistas como para las propias comunidades. Entre 2011 y 2026 se registraron 12.588 procesos de consulta previa, y de aquellos iniciados entre 2022 y 2026, apenas el 16 % llegó a protocolización, mientras que el 77 % permanece activo en Colombia. Según Citi ( C ), América Latina cuenta con las mayores reservas globales de cobre y litio, lideró las inversiones globales en exploración minera en 2025 y se proyecta que su mercado de minerales alcance un valor de US$130.000 millones en minería y US$24.000 millones en refinación para el año 2040. A pesar de este potencial, el rol de la región continúa siendo mayoritariamente extractivo o “aguas arriba” ( upstream ). La brecha respecto a las grandes potencias industriales es inmensa: mientras Chile refina aproximadamente 1,7 millones de toneladas (Mt) de cobre, China procesa cerca de 14 Mt. Adicionalmente, el escenario base de la Agencia Internacional de la Energía (AIE) estima que los proyectos actualmente anunciados cubrirían apenas el 76% de la demanda global de cobre y el 68% de la de litio para 2035. “Dado que este déficit no responde a una falta de reservas físicas sino a cuellos de botella en la ejecución de proyectos (infraestructura, demoras regulatorias y estructuración financiera), el desenlace de esta coyuntura histórica no está predeterminado”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea en una reciente entrevista el economista William Husband, director Global de Banca Corporativa de Metales y Minería del Citi. Ver más: Los países con los precios de la gasolina más altos y bajos en América Latina al comenzar el cuarto trimestre de 2026

item.title: Qué hospitales de Costa Rica aparecen más en ChatGPT y otras IA, según un estudio
item.description: ¿Qué ocurre cuando un paciente pregunta a ChatGPT, Claude o Perplexity dónde atenderse? Un estudio analiza qué hospitales aparecen y cuánto de lo que dicen se puede comprobar.
item.dc:creator: Fátima Romero
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — Dos de los seis hospitales privados de Costa Rica, CIMA San José y Clínica Bíblica, concentran el 64,4% de las menciones en las respuestas que dan los asistentes de inteligencia artificial a quienes preguntan dónde atenderse. Ver más: Empleos remotos y globales: los perfiles latinos más demandados por la IA, según Alexander Torrenegra Es el principal resultado del primer índice de visibilidad hospitalaria en IA en América Latina, elaborado en el país centroamericano. “Los hospitales privados de Costa Rica compiten por pacientes locales, por residentes extranjeros y por el turismo médico de la región, y cada vez más de esos pacientes le preguntan primero a una inteligencia artificial dónde atenderse”, explicó el coautor del reporte Roberto Echeverría Cárdenas, quien es consultor en IA aplicada a la salud con más de 20 años de experiencia en el sector, incluido el Ministerio de Salud. Para medir cómo contesta la IA, el indicador, llamado Sextante, registró 14.112 respuestas de ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Meta AI y DeepSeek sobre seis hospitales privados del país, en español y en inglés, y las contrastó con las fuentes oficiales de cada institución. Luego midió qué información encuentran los pacientes cuando consultan a estos sistemas, no la calidad clínica de los hospitales. El reporte, dirigido por Sebastián Urbina Cañas, exvicepresidente de Inteligencia Artificial y Ciencia de Datos de Genpact y exviceministro de Transportes, cuenta con la asesoría médica de María Luisa Ávila Agüero, exministra de Salud. La medición parte de una pregunta cada vez más relevante para los hospitales: qué imagen recibe un paciente cuando recurre primero a una herramienta de IA en busca de información sobre dónde atenderse. Hasta ahora, según los autores, no existían datos comparables sobre esa etapa del proceso en Centroamérica. La tendencia ocurre mientras aumenta el uso de estas herramientas para buscar información sanitaria. En Estados Unidos, la proporción de adultos que utilizó chatbots con ese fin pasó del 16% en 2024 al 32% en 2025, según Rock Health. Además, el 63% de quienes habían visto respuestas de IA al buscar información de salud las consideró algo o muy confiables, de acuerdo con Annenberg. Las 14.112 respuestas se obtuvieron el 16 y 17 de agosto mediante nueve configuraciones de GPT-5.6 Luna (OpenAI), Gemini 3.6 Flash (Google), Claude Sonnet 5 (Anthropic), Sonar (Perplexity), Llama 4 Maverick (Meta) y DeepSeek V4 Flash. Ver más: Así funciona Health Assistant, el nuevo asistente de IA de Samsung para monitorear la salud Los hospitales evaluados en el estudio fueron CIMA San José, Clínica Bíblica, La Católica, Metropolitano, San Rafael Arcángel, en Liberia, y UNIBE. El puntaje de cada uno consideró presencia en las respuestas (40%), exactitud y especificidad (30%) y reputación expresada por los modelos (30%). Según los hallazgos, hay diferencias entre ser reconocido y aparecer espontáneamente. UNIBE fue mencionada en el 5,4% de las preguntas abiertas, pero alcanzó 87,6 puntos sobre 100 cuando los modelos fueron consultados directamente sobre esa institución. En cuanto a la precisión, en CIMA, el 1,1% de las 4.027 respuestas analizadas contenía al menos un error en alguno de esos aspectos, frente al 4,5% de las 3.664 respuestas sobre Clínica Bíblica. La proporción fue mayor en Metropolitano, con un 28,7% de 1.202 respuestas, y en La Católica, con un 23,5% de 1.690. El análisis también detectó que los modelos pueden reproducir información desactualizada. Las nueve configuraciones estudiadas describieron como operativo, al menos en una ocasión, un hospital que permanece cerrado desde 2018. La frecuencia con que apareció esa información osciló entre el 1,4% y el 5,9% de las 1.568 respuestas analizadas para cada configuración. Los resultados variaron además según el modelo de inteligencia artificial utilizado y si tenía acceso a búsqueda en internet. Las respuestas con algún error fueron desde el 7,6% en GPT-5.6 Luna con búsqueda web, sobre 1.322 respuestas, hasta el 40,4% en DeepSeek V4 Flash sin búsqueda, sobre 997 respuestas. Los autores prevén seguir cada mes la evolución de la visibilidad hospitalaria en la región, conforme se actualicen los sistemas y la información disponible, con la intención de ampliar posteriormente el análisis de otros países de América Latina.

item.title: Eleitores vão às urnas com expectativa de resultado apertado entre Lula e Flávio em eleição polarizada
item.description: Marcada por polêmicas envolvendo desde o Judiciário até a padroeira do Brasil, passando por denúncias generalizadas de corrupção e temores de interferência externa, a campanha eleitoral para a Presidência da República chega ao primeiro turno, neste domingo, com a disputa totalmente em aberto entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), em mais um pleito marcado pela polarização.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões
item.content:encoded: Marcada por polêmicas envolvendo desde o Judiciário até a padroeira do Brasil, passando por denúncias generalizadas de corrupção e temores de interferência externa, a campanha eleitoral para a Presidência da República chega ao primeiro turno, neste domingo, com a disputa totalmente em aberto entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), em mais um pleito marcado pela polarização. Os mais de 158,7 milhões de brasileiros aptos a votar começaram a ir às seções eleitorais nesta manhã -- as urnas abriram às 8h e fecham às 17h pelo horário de Brasília -- após meses de embates muitas vezes em nível pessoal de cada lado, em que as propostas para governar o país pelos próximos quatro anos não foram protagonistas. Lula e Flávio votaram no começo da manhã e manifestaram confiança na vitória. Ao votar em uma escola em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), Lula fez um apelo para que os eleitores com mais de 70 anos compareçam às urnas e reafirmou que o que está em jogo nas eleições é a escolha entre o "fortalecimento do regime democrático e a barbárie". Flávio Bolsonaro votou em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, pouco após a abertura das urnas, e disse que espera vencer já no primeiro turno. "As nossas pesquisas internas mostram que a gente ultrapassou no primeiro turno já faz algum tempo", declarou. "Espero que seja suficiente para dar vitória no primeiro turno." As pesquisas de intenção de voto divulgadas no sábado, no entanto, apontam para uma nova rodada de votação, que aconteceria em 25 de outubro. Para a eleição acabar neste domingo, é preciso que um dos candidatos conquiste mais de 50% dos votos válidos, quando são desconsiderados os votos brancos e nulos. Levantamentos do Datafolha e da Quaest colocaram Lula e Flávio em empate técnico no primeiro turno nos votos válidos, com vantagem numérica do atual presidente de 3 pontos na primeira e de 1 ponto na segunda. Uma outra pesquisa, do MDA, colocou Lula com 47,8% dos votos válidos contra 42,1% de Flávio. O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou confiar em um processo tranquilo de votação: "Amanhecemos o dia hoje com a segurança de que as eleições vão transcorrer na maior normalidade", disse, ao votar em Brasília. A campanha chegou ao fim sem que Lula e Flávio tenham se enfrentado diretamente. No debate da TV Bandeirantes, ambos decidiram não ir, deixando os púlpitos vazios com seus nomes para serem criticados por Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão) e Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), que estavam presentes. Romeu Zema (Novo) completa a lista dos outros candidatos cujos partidos têm representação no Congresso, mas cujas intenções de voto jamais se aproximaram da dos dois líderes. Já o debate da TV Globo, que tradicionalmente encerra as campanhas, acabou sendo [USN:L1N45N18V TEXT:"cancelado"] após uma série de decisões judiciais e da desistência de última hora de Flávio, filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro -- que está atualmente em prisão domiciliar após ser condenado por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Lula havia dito dias antes que não compareceria. TEMOR DE INTERFERÊNCIA A eleição também ocorre em meio a renovados temores sobre uma possível interferência estrangeira na eleição presidencial brasileira. A Reuters [USN:L6N45M0VR TEXT:"revelou"] na última semana que autoridades francesas e alemãs ouviram de membros da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) que já estariam acontecendo tentativas de interferência dos Estados Unidos e da Rússia no pleito. Além disso, na quinta-feira, a embaixada dos EUA no Brasil [USN:L6N45O0XD TEXT:"anunciou"] a suspensão dos serviços consulares a partir da última sexta-feira, alegando preocupações não especificadas de segurança. Além disso, a embaixada pediu aos seus funcionários que trabalhassem de casa na sexta após uma ameaça. A embaixadora da Austrália também anunciou o fechamento da representação diplomática do país em Brasília citando o alerta norte-americano. A medida foi criticada pelo presidente do PT, Edinho Silva, que viu tentativa do governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de influenciar a opinião pública brasileira. A relação com os EUA e com Trump foi, inclusive, um dos principais marcadores da diferença entre Lula e Flávio. Enquanto o presidente alertou o homólogo norte-americano publicamente a não interferir no Brasil, o senador procurou mostrar proximidade com Trump, inclusive visitando-o na Casa Branca. "É uma relação tensa porque o Brasil não quer se ver dentro da zona de influência dos EUA. Tradicionalmente a nossa diplomacia é independente. O Lula acredita que, pela boa relação com a China, especialmente a comercial, que manter essa independência é fundamental", disse Leonardo Barreto, cofundador da Think Policy. "O Flávio tenta fazer dos EUA uma espécie de fiador das eleições. A família Bolsonaro acredita que as eleições não são feitas em condições de liberdade. Desconfiança em relação a urna, meios de comunicação, administração do Judiciário. Buscam no apoio dos americanos uma espécie de pressão para garantir o mínimo de neutralidade das autoridades brasileiras, percebem nos americanos uma espécie de seguro", acrescentou. BETS, STF E PADROEIRA Em meio a denúncias de corrupção como as do Banco Master e o escândalo do INSS, que atingiram tanto Flávio quanto o filho mais velho de Lula, além de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a campanha também foi marcada pelo apelo do senador ao seu pai, ao mesmo tempo em que buscava se mostrar mais moderado do que o ex-presidente, enquanto Lula seguiu batendo na tecla dos seus três mandatos na Presidência e lançando mão de medidas populares às vésperas do pleito. Entre elas, o governo anunciou o reajuste de 15% nos benefícios do Bolsa Família, a edição de uma medida provisória para proibir as casas de apostas online, as chamadas bets, e o anúncio da intenção de distribuir gratuitamente pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) as chamadas canetas emagrecedoras, três medidas aprovadas pelo eleitorado, segundo as pesquisas de opinião. Mas a polêmica que marcou a reta final da campanha ficou por conta de rumores de que Flávio retiraria de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil, o que foi negado com veemência pelo senador. Flávio classificou os boatos de "fake news", enquanto Lula disse que, enquanto for presidente, ninguém irá "avacalhar" com Nossa Senhora. Além do presidente, os eleitores também escolherão neste domingo os governadores dos 26 Estados e do Distrito Federal, além de 54 dos 81 senadores e dos 513 deputados e dos integrantes das Assembleias Legislativa de 26 Estado e da Câmara Distrital do Distrito Federal. A eleição para o Senado estará sob o foco, em um momento de pressão sobre ministros do STF, que podem sofrer impeachment pelos integrantes da Casa, e em um momento em que estão [USN:L6N45N0ZL TEXT:"vagas"] funções em órgãos reguladores, como o Banco Central, cujos nomes precisam ser aprovados pelo Senado.

item.title: Verstappen wins chaotic rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
item.description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday for his first victory of the season after the race start was delayed by more than 90 minutes due to treacherous conditions at the Sepang International Circuit.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday for his first victory of the season after the race start was [USN:L1N45Q01D TEXT:"delayed by more than 90 minutes"] due to treacherous conditions at the Sepang International Circuit. Verstappen was the last driver to win in Sepang in 2017 before it was taken off the calendar and the Dutchman, who had also taken pole, gave Red Bull a first victory with their own power unit despite an early setback when he lost the lead before turn one. "It's a really nice one after the year that we've had and the progression that we've made. So I'm incredibly proud of everyone. It is super nice to win here," said Verstappen. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second for Mercedes and now has an 84-point lead over his closest rival and teammate George Russell, who was third when he retired with a suspected power unit issue with five laps remaining. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished third despite a tyre gamble that had dropped the Briton down to 18th at the start of the race. "Obviously, we had the wrong call at the beginning, which was so difficult and I could see everyone just pulling away," Hamilton said. "I thought that was kind of race over for us, but I just kept my head down. The guys did a great job with the pit stops." Antonelli held on to second from Hamilton in the closing laps. "Today was the maximum we could have done... On our side, a lot of work to do," Antonelli said. "We've been struggling a bit more than usual, but still really happy to come away with P2." The last four laps were a straight shootout for podium places after a lengthy safety car period and that was when Hamilton, who had been chasing Red Bull's Isack Hadjar for several laps, made his move. Charles Leclerc, who had also been closer to the back of the grid at the start of the race amid the chaos of a wet track, salvaged fourth for Ferrari when he overtook Hadjar with two laps to go. Hadjar finished fifth ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Liam Lawson was seventh while Fernando Alonso was eighth for Aston Martin, their best result of the season. FIRST WET RACE OF 2026 The season had not yet had a wet race where the 2026 cars could be tested and the rain - which had stayed away in practice and qualifying - arrived with heavy showers sweeping across the circuit, delaying the start. After a suspended start procedure, the second start had drivers split between intermediate and slick tyres but it was the former that thrived early in the race. When the lights went out, Antonelli accelerated through the middle from third on the grid to take the lead from Verstappen while Russell shot past on the outside to move up from seventh to second. But Verstappen's recovery began on lap six when he attacked Russell, overtaking the Briton by diving down the inside of turn four to set his sights on Antonelli. The Italian had to defend his position until lap 10 when Valtteri Bottas spun his Cadillac into the gravel, bringing out the safety car as Verstappen pitted while the two Mercedes cars double stacked to switch to slick tyres. VERSTAPPEN TAKES LEAD When the safety car came in, Verstappen stayed glued to Antonelli's rear tyre before overtaking the Italian on turn three, with Russell also surging past his team mate on the next turn to flip the order. Verstappen looked comfortable setting the pace up front as he set fastest laps and extended his lead over Russell to over four seconds as a frustrated Antonelli informed the team that he had the pace to chase the Dutchman. An impatient Antonelli overtook Russell on lap 21 to move up to second while behind them Hamilton had quietly been chipping away on his ageing soft tyres to move up to fifth behind Hadjar. But Antonelli missed his braking point at turn 15 and went briefly off track, hitting the pit lane bollard and costing him valuable time as Verstappen extended his lead to eight seconds. When the second safety car came out towards the end for Alex Albon's Williams that was stuck in the gravel, Russell suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he got out of the car with a suspected power unit issue.

item.title: OPEC+ agrees to keep November oil output targets steady
item.description: OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November at a meeting on Sunday, the producer group said, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Alex Lawler, Olesya Astakhova
item.content:encoded: OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November at a meeting on Sunday, the producer group said, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year. Seven core members of the group comprising the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia made the decision for November in a brief online meeting on Sunday. The core members are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman. Gulf OPEC+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran , with exports fluctuating at 60% to 80% of normal levels in recent months. "The OPEC+ group of seven kept their production ceilings unchanged, in line with market expectations. That said, despite rising flows through the Strait of Hormuz, their output levels remain well below quota," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo. "Consequently, the oil market remains tight." Oil prices had dropped on Friday after European leaders agreed to US President Donald Trump's request to release diesel reserves. Even so, Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel, up from about $73 before the Iran war started in late February. OUTPUT HIKES HAVE BEEN LARGELY ON PAPER THIS YEAR The Iran war has also delayed the group's output [USN:L6N45O0QD TEXT:"capacity review"] — crucial to determine members’ 2027 output quotas — because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources told Reuters last week. OPEC+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases stayed on paper because of the Middle East conflict. The seven core OPEC+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February, OPEC data shows. The seven hold their next meeting on November 1. OPEC+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs the result of the capacity review to decide how to distribute increases and any [USN:L6N43U0TI TEXT:"changes to output are unlikely"] before 2027, sources have said. A separate OPEC+ ministerial group called the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC), which does not decide policy, also met on Sunday to review the market.

item.title: Asian Games close after fortnight of turmoil and teenage triumph
item.description: The 20th Asian Games closed on Sunday after a rocky fortnight lit up by youthful brilliance in the sporting arenas but tempered by logistical dysfunction and subdued public interest.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: The 20th Asian Games closed on Sunday after a rocky fortnight lit up by youthful brilliance in the sporting arenas but tempered by logistical dysfunction and subdued public interest. Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani declared the Games closed at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, with the torch handed to organisers of the next event in Doha 2030. Some 17,000 athletes and officials came for the Aichi-Nagoya showpiece, more than the Paris Olympics, competing in 469 gold-medal events spanning Tokyo to Osaka. The massive scale clashed with organisers' planning for a "simple, streamlined and functional event" -- and the results were often chaotic. Athletes and teams complained of bungled accommodation and transport, prompting repeated apologies from the embarrassed organising committee. Despite the challenges, the Games were lifted by the performances of teenage titans, led by China's 13-year-old swimmer Yu Zidi. Awarded the female Most Valuable Player of the Games, Yu is on track for a huge Los Angeles Olympics after claiming three individual gold medals in the Tokyo pool. She swam the second-fastest time [USN:L6N45D0EU TEXT:"in winning the 200 metres individual medley, setting up a battle royale with Canada's world-record holder Summer McIntosh"]. Her 19-year-old teammate Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer to win seven golds at the Games, while Japan's 17-year-old wunderkind Shin Ohashi [USN:L6N45G0U5 TEXT:"smashed the 200m breaststroke world record"]. Youthful brilliance lit up the athletics, with China's 18-year-old Yan Ziyi producing a world-class throw to win the women's javelin gold while 20-year-old [USN:L6N45J03D TEXT:"Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson"] swept the 100 and 200m to become the men's MVP. NO GAMES VILLAGE The athletes performed despite regular logistical failures and occasional diplomatic gaffes. "Accommodation, transport and other issues -- it seems a lot of teams were affected," Hong Kong team chef de mission Wong Po-kee told Reuters on Sunday. Organisers opted to house athletes and officials in a mix of hotels, wooden container units and a cruise ship to cut costs rather than build a dedicated athletes' village. They budgeted for 15,000 athletes and officials -- about 2,000 fewer than total registrations -- and struggled to manage them. Waves of athletes spent up to 12 hours waiting to be registered on arrival. When checking in, some found their rooms double-booked or being shared by the wrong teammates. Transport problems dogged the Games throughout, with athletes' shuttle buses failing to turn up or taking them to the wrong venues. Several competitions were delayed by the errors. South Korea's delegation were particularly aggrieved, with their team chef de mission [USN:L6N45G0EP TEXT:"marking the Games' organisation with an 'F"]'. Their men's soccer team were upset when the South Korean flag was unable to be hoisted for the national anthem at the victory ceremony after they beat Japan for the gold medal on Saturday. The North Korean national anthem played for South Korea's men's hockey team earlier in the Games in another awkward mix-up. Five years after the Tokyo Olympics was staged without fans due to COVID-19 restrictions, Japan's first major multi-sport event was blighted by poor crowds. Fewer than 1,000 spectators watched the hosts beat South Korea in the women's soccer semi-finals at a 50,000-capacity stadium. Much smaller venues were often nearly empty, though many were based in far-flung locations, making access a challenge. "If I had to say, well, I don't think it was a success," Nagoya resident Naoko Toda, who watched several competitions, told Reuters before the closing ceremony. Despite the issues, the Games' governing OCA declared Aichi-Nagoya [USN:L6N45Q019 TEXT:"a success"] and praised organisers for their frugal arrangements. China topped the table with 169 golds among 341 medals, their best haul at an overseas Asian Games. But Japan also delivered for fans who tuned in, with 83 golds in a total of 269 medals, smashing their previous record at Hiroshima 1994. Padel, mixed martial arts, teqball and surfing made their Games debuts in a record 43-sport programme that dwarfed the Paris Olympics. Qatar is set to host the next Asiad in 2030, though the OCA may elect to [USN:L6N45N0IY TEXT:"push it back a year"] to serve as the continent's Olympic qualifiers before Brisbane 2032.

item.title: US Supreme Court to kick off term with bid by Big Oil to toss climate suits
item.description: Monday's arguments mark the latest example of energy-sector companies asking the justices to block climate-related liability or limit federal environmental regulation.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel, Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court begins its new nine-month term on Monday with arguments in [USN:L1N45G0O2 TEXT:"a major case"] involving a bid by oil companies ExxonMobil (XOM.N) and Suncor Energy (SU.TO) to scuttle a lawsuit by officials in Boulder, Colorado, seeking monetary damages for harms caused by climate change. It is the first of several important cases already teed up for the term, with disputes involving issues such as President Donald Trump 's [USN:S0N43101E TEXT:"immigration policies"] and state-level bans on [USN:S0N3YR01V TEXT:"assault-style rifles"] to be heard in the coming months. The court's 6-3 conservative majority has moved US law dramatically rightward in recent years. The top US judicial body, as is its custom, opens its term on the first Monday in October. US-based Exxon and Canada-based Suncor appealed after the Colorado Supreme Court let Boulder's lawsuit accusing them of state law violations proceed. The Trump administration has backed Exxon and Suncor, arguing that federal law precludes Boulder's claims. Boulder's city and county governments have accused the two companies of helping drive climate change and misleading the public about the risks of fossil fuels. Boulder aims to hold the companies liable for past and future costs associated with climate change such as infrastructure repairs, environmental damage, emergency management and harms to public health. The burning of fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases including carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, trapping heat and raising average global temperatures over time. Nearly 60 state and local governments have brought similar suits seeking billions of dollars from fossil fuel companies, with more continuing to be filed, Exxon and Suncor told the justices. A ruling by the Supreme Court in favor of the companies could lead to many of those cases being dismissed. Monday's arguments mark the latest example of energy-sector companies asking the justices to block climate-related liability or limit federal environmental regulation. Backers of the oil companies argue that if Boulder's most far-reaching claims are allowed to proceed, it could give states sweeping power over conduct occurring far outside their borders. Energy companies and trade groups, along with states allied with them, have built a largely winning record before the justices over the past two decades in cases involving climate liability and the reach of federal environmental regulation. Exxon and Suncor argue, among other things, that Boulder's claims intrude on an area governed by the Clean Air Act. Justice Samuel Alito [USN:L1N45K0QH TEXT:"has recused"] himself from participating in the case. Alito owns stock in several oil and gas companies but not Exxon or Suncor, according to his financial disclosure forms. The Supreme Court's decision is expected by the end of June.

item.title: Brazilians head to polls in high-stakes, polarized election
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, is seeking a fourth term as president while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle
item.content:encoded: Brazilians head to the polls on Sunday in the first round of a narrowly split election after a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling. Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 80, is seeking a fourth term, while Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power. A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's reelection could create a headache for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security. Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign has offered meager policy debate, as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates. If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes, the top two will face off on October 25. Surveys show Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro polling roughly even in a likely runoff. Other candidates, including former state governors Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, have struggled to break through with the polarized electorate, even as Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro are each rejected by roughly half of voters, polls show. Flavio Bolsonaro has promised to seek amnesty for his father, who is serving a sentence of more than 27 years for plotting a coup after his narrow election defeat in 2022. Lula has cast the election as a choice between "democracy and denialism" and repeatedly warned of foreign interference. THE TRUMP FACTOR The fallout from Jair Bolsonaro's conviction last year has colored much of the campaign. Trump, who called that case a "witch hunt," imposed a 50% tariff on Brazil in 2025, [USN:FWN3T60MV TEXT:"explicitly linking the tariffs to the trial of Bolsonaro"] after lobbying from the Bolsonaro family to pressure Brazil's Supreme Court to drop the charges. This year, Trump levied new tariffs over alleged unfair trade practices. Lula has cast the move as an attempt to sway the election and portrayed the Bolsonaros as too eager to please Washington at Brazil's expense. Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins. They point to a failed effort to send US officials to Brazil in order to "discuss electoral integrity," according to the US State Department. Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"alleged US and Russian interference"] before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs. Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly. The senator, who has pledged closer ties with the US and Israel, welcomed the Trump administration's designation of Brazil's major gangs as terrorist groups, which Lula rejected. Also in play is US access to Brazil's vast critical mineral reserves, key to Washington's push to reduce dependence on China for those materials. ECONOMIC HEADWINDS Despite [USN:L1N44111S TEXT:"falling inequality"] and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"high living costs"], heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity. Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families. Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's president may need to address. The government lowered its [USN:S0N42R02G TEXT:"economic growth forecasts"] for this year and next to just 2.0% and 2.3% respectively. "Lula would likely preserve a state-led model with only modest spending restraint; Bolsonaro would likely pursue a more market-friendly agenda centered on spending cuts, privatizations, concessions, and a stronger fiscal anchor," said Alberto Ramos, chief Latin America economist at Goldman Sachs. SCANDAL-PLAGUED CAMPAIGN Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil's political class and renewed public anger over corruption. Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker's ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Flavio Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police. The senator has denied any wrongdoing, although he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Vorcaro to make a movie about his father. The banker's connections to Moraes, seen by many as a Lula ally, [USN:L6N44U1B6 TEXT:"plunged the court into crisis"] a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the president. Moraes has said the case is politically and electorally motivated for [USN:L1N4560NZ TEXT:"his conviction of the elder Bolsonaro"]. Lula has also tried to distance himself from a federal police investigation into his son over alleged influence peddling, which his son denies. On Sunday, voters will also elect all 513 lower house members and two-thirds of the Senate, where some lawmakers have pushed to impeach Moraes. Congress has gained greater influence in Brazilian politics since the impeachment of former President Dilma Rousseff, a Lula ally, in 2016, raising the stakes of those legislative races.

item.title: Like a 'vertical roller coaster': Simulating flight FZ1073's sudden plunge
item.description: A prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe, an expert says.
item.dc:creator: Ben Makori
item.content:encoded: Flydubai's [USN:S8N44D013 TEXT:"flight FZ1073"], which plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, would have felt like a "vertical roller coaster", according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters. The steep fall, after an attack on the captain by the co-pilot during a flight on Wednesday, would have put huge strain on the Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft - as well as the passengers and crew, said Alberto Paduanelli, owner of ALPA Simulation in Sherfield on Loddon, southern England. The co-pilot of the flydubai jet, which was bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"terrorist attack"]". The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, two sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity. Reuters could not independently reach al-Hammami for comment. Flydubai says the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation and it cannot comment further. Oman has yet to comment on the incident. "A plunge of 16,000 feet (4,877 metres) over 30 seconds will feel like you are over on a very, very vertical roller coaster," Paduanelli said, sitting at the controls of the simulator cockpit. "The difference is that on the roller coaster, you know what's happening," he said, adding that with a sudden drop "you feel the negative g-force on your body". For passengers who are not strapped in, "Your body will literally lift from the seat", he said. Using a simulator to recreate the incident, Paduanelli said the aircraft's autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing the jet to accelerate rapidly. US President Donald Trump has praised the Boeing jet for withstanding the severe forces put on it during the incident. The plane was levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, before a reserve crew of pilots onboard landed the plane. "It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural planning and design," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that the 737 Max "was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do". Boeing did not respond to a request for comment. Aircraft are designed and tested to withstand substantial aerodynamic loads, but Paduanelli said a prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe. "This was nothing but a miracle that nothing was hurt apart from the captain, unfortunately, and that two pilots were onboard," Paduanelli said. Details about al-Hammami's past have trickled out. Royal Air Maroc told Reuters he did a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. Buckinghamshire New University in Britain said he did a distance-learning course in aviation management with the institution, but no pilot training. An Australian Federal Police spokesperson said on Sunday that authorities there were investigating al-Hammami's "links to Australia". A source briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne.

item.title: Philippines accuses Chinese coast guard of blocking law enforcement mission near Thitu
item.description: The Philippine Coast Guard said on Sunday Chinese vessels obstructed a Philippine law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near the Manila-held Thitu Island in the South China Sea.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philippine Coast Guard said on Sunday Chinese vessels obstructed a Philippine law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near the Manila-held Thitu Island in the South China Sea. It described the presence of a Chinese navy helicopter as an "unnecessary act of intimidation". It was the latest in a series of [USN:L6N45N0JJ TEXT:"recent maritime confrontations"] between Manila and Beijing. The operation involved personnel from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Philippine Navy and Philippine National Police Maritime Group responding to a report of suspected blast fishing near Sandy Cays 2 and 3, about three nautical miles west of Thitu Island, known in the Philippines as Pag-asa. The PCG said two China Coast Guard vessels sounded their horns, radio-challenged the Philippine team and later shadowed and blocked its boats. A People's Liberation Army Navy helicopter also circled above the Philippine personnel four times. The Philippine team ordered the foreign fishing vessel to stop and radioed it several times, but the vessel ignored the orders and sailed southwest toward Subi Reef, one of seven artificial islands China has built in the Spratlys to support its sovereignty claims. Philippine authorities ended the pursuit for safety reasons and returned to Thitu. The PCG said the China Coast Guard had "no law enforcement authority" in the territorial sea of Thitu and said its actions "made it easier for a suspected violator to escape". It also rejected any Chinese claim that its vessels had been expelled from the area. At just 37 hectares (0.14 square miles), the coral-fringed Thitu is the largest and most prized of the nine Philippines-held features in the Spratly archipelago, located 450 km (280 miles) from the mainland. Separately, the military said a Chinese J-16 fighter jet repeatedly approached and manoeuvred close to a Philippine patrol aircraft over the disputed Scarborough Shoal on Saturday, creating an aviation safety risk. The Armed Forces of the Philippines said the incident was part of a "recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behaviour" against Philippine vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations. The Chinese Embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the weekend incidents.

item.title: Modric 'ashamed' after England hand Croatia worst defeat in their history
item.description: Croatia's Luka Modric said he was ashamed of his side's performance after they lost 7-0 to England in Rijeka on Saturday, the heaviest defeat in their history.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Croatia's Luka Modric said he was ashamed of his side's performance after they lost 7-0 to England in Rijeka on Saturday, the heaviest defeat in their history. Croatia's previous heaviest loss was a 6-0 defeat by Spain in 2018. Modric, the country's most-capped player, said the manner of the defeat by [USN:L6N45P06Q TEXT:"England"] was unacceptable. "It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance without duels, fouls, aggressiveness, togetherness... I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time I feel ashamed after a game," he told Jutarnji. "You can lose, or play against an opponent who is better - and they are right now. But in any case, losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable. "You can't play football like that. You can't play with two players less, you can't play like this, and we looked like we had 4-5 players less. A catastrophic night," the 41-year-old added. Croatia next host Spain in Split on Tuesday. The world champions have a 100% record so far in the Nations League and won their first meeting 4-1 on Tuesday. "We need to pull ourselves together, stay together because a new difficult game awaits us," said Modric. "And we have to show our true colours, that there is defiance and pride in us, desire, willingness, togetherness, these things cannot be lost overnight." Croatia are third in Nations League A, Group Three.

item.title: Two dead in flooding in Spain's Catalonia region
item.description: Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday. Catalan leader Salvador Illa confirmed the death of a man after a wall collapsed in Tordera, a town to the north of Barcelona, in a message on his social media account on Sunday. Another person died in Montornès del Vallès, firefighters said on Sunday, while emergency services were searching for a missing person in Pineda de Mar, a town 52 km (32 miles) to the north of Barcelona. Catalan authorities issued a red alert warning and urged people to stay inside from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Saturday until Sunday at 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) because a "mini-hurricane" could hit the northeastern region, with more heavy rain forecast. Homes were flooded and cars left submerged in Bellvitge and Cornella near Barcelona after torrential rain on Saturday. Ducks swam in huge puddles that formed on motorways in Barcelona. Sarai Sarroca, director of regional weather service Meteocat, said on Saturday that the core of an exceptional weather system was over the Mediterranean and a "mini-hurricane" could move over land in Catalonia. Flights were cancelled or delayed at Barcelona airport, La Vanguardia newspaper reported on Saturday. All local trains were disrupted by the deluge. Shops shut early, football matches were called off and a performance of Verdi's Aida at Barcelona's Liceu opera house was cancelled.

item.title: US carrier George H W Bush visits Thailand after Middle East deployment
item.description: The carrier arrived in Phuket on Sunday with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

US carrier George H W Bush visits Thailand after Middle East deployment

The carrier arrived in Phuket on Sunday with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East.

FAST

PHUKET: The United States aircraft carrier George H W Bush arrived in Thailand's resort island of Phuket on Sunday (Oct 4) with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East.

For the last six months, the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier and its strike group supported Operation Epic Fury and the US naval blockade in the US Central Command area of responsibility to secure maritime security and stability in the Middle East, according to the US Navy.

Phuket is the first port call for the George H W Bush Carrier Strike Group since departing Norfolk, Virginia, and Mayport, Florida, in March, the US Navy said in a statement.

Sailors will take part in cultural and community activities in Phuket, including sightseeing tours and a US-Thailand soccer match, it said.

The carrier anchored offshore, while crew members are expected to come ashore through Phuket Deep Sea Port and spend time on the popular southern resort island from Oct 4 to 9, local media reported.

Some sailors were seen coming ashore by boat.

The visit follows a five-day port call by the US carrier Abraham Lincoln at Laem Chabang in eastern Thailand last month, with about 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard.

A local mayor had estimated each US service member from the Lincoln could spend up to 3,000 baht ($89) per day during the visit.

Thailand is the United States' only treaty ally in mainland Southeast Asia.

item.title: Le Premier ministre letton en passe de diriger une coalition pro-ukrainienne
item.description: Le Premier ministre letton, Andris Kulbergs, devrait conserver le pouvoir, sa "Liste unie", formation centriste et pro-ukrainienne, étant en passe de signer une large victoire, la plus importante aux élections législatives depuis que la Lettonie a retrouvé son indépendance en 1991.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas
item.content:encoded: Le Premier ministre letton, Andris Kulbergs, devrait conserver le pouvoir, sa "Liste unie", formation centriste et pro-ukrainienne, étant en passe de signer une large victoire, la plus importante aux élections législatives depuis que la Lettonie a retrouvé son indépendance en 1991. Après 97% des bulletins dépouillés après le scrutin de samedi dans ce pays membre de l'Otan et de l'Union européenne, frontalier de la Russie, la Liste unie recueillait 35,3% des voix, ce qui lui permettait d'obtenir 42 sièges au Parlement, qui en compte 100. Andris Kulbergs, homme d'affaires et pilote de rallye amateur âgé de 47 ans, est arrivé au pouvoir en mai après l'effondrement de la [USN:L6N41R0M0 TEXT:"coalition précédente"], en raison de la manière dont cette dernière avait géré des incidents au cours desquels des drones militaires avaient pénétré dans l'espace aérien letton sans être détectés. Tout au long de sa campagne, il a promis de renforcer les capacités anti-drones de la Lettonie et de maintenir les dépenses de défense à 5% du produit intérieur brut (PIB), l'un des niveaux les plus élevés des membres de l'Otan. La Lettonie, qui compte 1,9 million d'habitants, longe la mer Baltique, avec au nord et au sud l'Estonie et la Lituanie, alliées de l'UE et de l'Otan, et à l'est la Russie et la Biélorussie. Alors que l'économie lettone affiche des résultats inférieurs à ceux de ses voisins baltes depuis plus d'une décennie, Andris Kulbergs s'est engagé à améliorer la gouvernance, à alléger les formalités administratives et à réduire les dépenses publiques, a déclaré le politologue Roberts Kits. "Kulbergs a misé sur son image d'homme d'action et a convaincu les électeurs qu'il pouvait faire les choses différemment, apporter un vent de fraîcheur", a-t-il expliqué. "Cela signifie que la responsabilité est énorme. Les gens attendent de lui qu'il tienne ses promesses, mais la question reste de savoir s'il dispose de l'équipe nécessaire pour y parvenir." Liste unie devrait être en mesure d'obtenir une majorité parlementaire soit avec l'Alliance nationale, parti nationaliste, soit avec les Progressistes, parti libéral, a estime Roberts Kits. LIGNE DURE CONTRE LA RUSSIE Andris Kulbergs s'est engagé à continuer de soutenir l'Ukraine et à maintenir une ligne dure envers Moscou. "Tout lien économique avec la Russie nous affaiblit. Certes, cela peut rapporter un peu d'argent supplémentaire, mais c'est une faiblesse dont la Russie pourrait tirer parti", a-t-il déclaré aux journalistes au siège de son parti le soir des élections, alors que ses partisans célébraient déjà la victoire écrasante de sa formation. "C'est extrêmement élevé. Je ne m'attendais pas à un tel résultat", a déclaré Andris Kulbergs Le taux de participation s'est élevé à 51,8%, en baisse par rapport au taux de 59,4% enregistré en 2022. Dans les résultats provisoires, après Liste unie, vient le parti populiste "Lettonie d'abord" qui a recueilli 13,1% des voix. Cette dernière formation, qui s'inspire du courant MAGA comme aux Etats-Unis, avait courtisé la minorité ethnique russe du pays à l'approche du scrutin. En troisième position figure le parti pro-russe "Pouvoir souverain", avec 11,7% des voix, suivi de l'Alliance nationale, qui prône une ligne dure envers le Kremlin, avec 8,9% des suffrages.

item.title: Éthiopie-La capitale du Tigré sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales-sources
item.description: Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont rapporté à Reuters trois sources dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont rapporté à Reuters trois sources dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord. Le Front populaire de libération du Tigré (TPLF), qui dirige l'alliance d'opposition, a déclaré dans un communiqué publié sur Facebook qu'il s'était retiré de la capitale du Tigré, Mekelle, et que le gouvernement régional serait "temporairement transféré hors de Mekelle et opérerait depuis un autre endroit". Une source proche de la milice pro-gouvernementale, les Forces de paix du Tigré, a indiqué que ses combattants étaient entrés dans le centre de Mekelle samedi après-midi, suivis par l'armée éthiopienne. Une source humanitaire et un habitant de Mekelle, sous couvert d'anonymat, ont confirmé que la ville était désormais aux mains des forces gouvernementales. Le cabinet du Premier ministre Abiy Ahmed n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire. La prise de Mekelle par les forces pro-gouvernementales constitue une importante perte pour l'alliance d'opposition dirigée par le TPLF, qui avait lancé une vaste [USN:L8N45F0T4 TEXT:"offensive"] le 23 septembre contre l'armée éthiopienne. Les forces fédérales éthiopiennes et les combattants alliés ont lancé une contre-offensive rapide dans le Tigré, mais selon les analystes, ces combats — qui constituent la pire escalade depuis la guerre civile de 2020-2022 — risquent de dégénérer en un conflit régional plus vaste. Le gouvernement fédéral d'Addis-Abeba a rompu ses relations diplomatiques avec l'Érythrée la semaine dernière, l'accusant de soutenir l'alliance rebelle aux côtés du Soudan et de l'Égypte. Les trois pays rejettent ces accusations.

item.title: Rare police raid of Taipei gay bar sparks angry protest
item.description: Taipei police took in 51 people in for questioning and arrested the bar's owner.
item.dc:creator: Yimou Lee, Ann Wang
item.content:encoded: Around 100 members of Taipei's LGBTQ+ community protested on Sunday after police raided a gay bar the day before and detained its customers, a highly unusual move given that Taiwan prides itself on its liberal image and legal support for sexual minorities. Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019 in a first for Asia and is normally a bastion of tolerance in a region where LGBTQ+ rights are often either suppressed or outlawed. Taipei holds its main [USN:L4N3W50AF TEXT:"Pride"] event later this month, the largest in East Asia. Taipei police raided the Commander D gay bar in the city's Wanhua district on Saturday afternoon, taking 51 people in for questioning, and arresting the bar's owner. Reuters could not reach him for comment. Precinct spokesperson Chen Yu-cheng told Reuters police had acted on a search warrant for suspected "offences against public morality". Chen said the 51 people were suspected of violating a law that prohibits "wantonly exposing one's naked body or presenting a lascivious posture in a public place or publicly accessible place". Protesters marched peacefully but noisily to the precinct police station on Sunday afternoon. "They raided the place violently. It was very scary," one of those detained, who asked to be identified only by his family name Wen, told Reuters. The Taipei city government referred Reuters to a separate police statement, which said police received a complaint alleging that the bar could be violating public decency laws. Mayor Chiang Wan-an from the main opposition party, the Kuomintang, who faces an election next month, has previously attended Taipei Pride and expressed his support for the LGBTQ+ community. The precinct chief, who did not give his name, came out to speak to protesters briefly. "We respect the culture of a pluralistic society and will protect the rights of every citizen," he said, as protesters shouted their disapproval at him. Protester Kang Yang said he was angry the raid had happened, particularly during Pride month. "I'm not cool with this," he said. "This city used to claim that it was queer friendly." Taiwan was under martial law until 1987 and same-sex relations were a largely taboo issue at the time.

item.title: Government forces seize capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region from rebels
item.description: Ethiopian government forces and allied militias have regained control of the capital of Tigray, three sources told Reuters on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ethiopian government forces and allied militias have regained control of the capital of Tigray, three sources told Reuters on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern region. The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the opposition alliance, said in a statement posted on Facebook it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be "temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else." A source close to the pro-government militia, the Tigray Peace Forces, said its fighters entered the centre of Mekelle on Saturday afternoon, followed by the Ethiopian military. A humanitarian source and a Mekelle resident, who asked not to be named, confirmed the city was controlled by government forces. The prime minister's office did not respond immediately to a request for comment. LOSS OF MEKELLE A MAJOR BLOW FOR TPLF The taking of Mekelle by pro-government forces is a major loss for the opposition alliance led by the TPLF, which [USN:L6N45G0J2 TEXT:"launched a big offensive"] on September 23 against the Ethiopian military. Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have made a quick counterattack into Tigray, but analysts say the fighting — the worst escalation since a 2020-2022 civil war — threatens to escalate into a wider regional conflict. The federal government in Addis Ababa severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea last week, accusing it of supporting the rebel alliance alongside Sudan and Egypt. The three countries deny this.

item.title: Saudi Arabia quietly shelving NEOM Stadium, one of 2034 World Cup venues
item.description: Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it. The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM. NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was [USN:S8N40J01E TEXT:"no longer a priority"], and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled. However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely. NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority. The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction. RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format. Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities. MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters. According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold". The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033. Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis. Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it [USN:L1N45M0WE TEXT:"expected"] a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6% following a drop in oil activities. PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added. In January Reuters [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"reported"] that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba. Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy [USN:L1N40Y0DC TEXT:"later articulated"] by Saudi officials. Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The [USN:L6N43I0ZY TEXT:"Aramco Stadium"] in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale. Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

FAST

RIYADH/DUBAI, Oct 4 : Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it. The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM. NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was no longer a priority, and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled.

However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely. NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority. The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction. RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format. Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities.  MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters.  According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold".  The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033. Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis. Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it expected a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6 per cent following a drop in oil activities. PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added. In January Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba. Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy later articulated by Saudi officials. Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The Aramco Stadium in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale. Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Los 10 objetos más olvidados en Uber México: los teléfonos lideran
item.description: El Índice de Objetos Olvidados de la plataforma destaca que también se han olvidado una canasta de tacos y hasta un penacho.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Garrido
item.content:encoded: “Creo que lo dejé en el Uber…”. Si usas este servicio es posible que hayas olvidado algo después de un viaje. Y esto es tan frecuente que la compañía lanza desde hace 10 años su Índice de Objetos Olvidados. En su edición 2026, los teléfonos lideran el listado como el artículo que más dejan los pasajeros en México. Las carteras y bolsos están el segundo puesto, mientras que las llaves ocuparon el tercer lugar. Otros artículos de la lista incluyen audífonos y bocinas, ropa, lentes, dinero en efectivo y hasta computadoras. Pero además de los artículos cotidianos, el informe también registró objetos inusuales que han sido encontrados por los conductores como un penacho, un tambor africano y hasta 400 tacos de canasta, que tradicionalmente se colocan y transportan dentro de un cesto para mantenerlos calientes. También se han dejado carriolas, extensiones de cabello y hasta prótesis dentales. Elaborado a partir de los reportes de usuarios que dejan cosas, el Índice también rastrea los días en los que más se olvidan ciertos artículos. Los martes y viernes son “los días oficiales” para olvidar laptops, los miércoles suelen ser comunes para dejar cargadores de computadora y los lentes se dejan los lunes, jueves, sábado y domingo. El informe también registra los horarios en los que los clientes tienden a ser más olvidadizos. Los lunes el pico de olvidos ocurre entre 2 PM y 4PM y de 6PM a 8PM. Los viernes entre 7 y 9PM. Los sábados tiene un punto crítico a las 3 PM y de 7 a 10 PM. La madrugada del domingo también concentra muchas de las pérdidas. item.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met
item.description: Additional points remain to be communicated to the US, a foreign-ministry spokesperson said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven Iranian conditions set out in a June interim agreement with the US are met, state media reported Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf as saying on Sunday. Iran presented a proposal during the UN General Assembly under which the Strait of Hormuz waterway could be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days if the conditions were met, with the US replying to this proposal last week via Qatari intermediaries. "The position of the Islamic Republic of Iran is completely clear and firm, and the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until our seven conditions, based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met," Qalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, was quoted as saying. He said Washington "must understand that the period of dragging out the (diplomatic) process and dictating one-sided demands is over". IRAN SAYS NO NUCLEAR DISCUSSIONS A Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had clarified its broad positions via mediators to the US response but that additional points remained to be communicated to Washington. "The Americans' propositions are more or less in line with their previous positions, specifically on the nuclear issue. We told them our focus in this stage is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz and the return to security in this waterway requires clear steps from the US," spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said. He also denied Tehran had offered UN nuclear watchdog inspections of its nuclear facilities in exchange for US sanctions relief, saying Iran had not entered into nuclear discussions with Washington. The [USN:L1N45M06A TEXT:"document being circulated"] outlines a seven-day period of trust-building aimed at returning the two sides to an enhanced version of the memorandum of understanding agreed in June, including concrete steps on Iran's nuclear programme, an official briefed on the talks said last week. The disagreement centres on the sequencing of the steps rather than the components of the plan, the official added. WARNING FROM ARAQCHI Qatar has been shuttling messages between Washington and Tehran in an effort to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war that began at the end of February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran. The June memorandum of understanding led to a brief ceasefire and included provisions on the strait and Iran's nuclear programme. Separately, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told foreign ambassadors and diplomats in Tehran on Sunday that Tehran hoped Washington would choose diplomacy but warned that Iran was prepared to respond if the US again chose military action. On Thursday, sources told Reuters that Iran was preparing a [USN:L8N45M1N4 TEXT:"broader and more forceful response"] if Washington resumed large-scale military attacks. “If they again move towards military solutions, we are more prepared than before and will take whatever action is necessary to defend ourselves,” Araqchi said on Sunday. Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia told Fars news agency on Sunday Iran would upgrade the range of its missiles.
