item.title: Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's 'new doctrine' of airstrikes, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Vladimir Putin called for broader attacks on civilian targets, Volodymyr Zelenskiy told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"force people to abandon Kyiv"] and other cities, but will not target civilians, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's intelligence services has obtained documents showing that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy said. "We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals," Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview. "To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation." Driving the shift in policy, Zelenskiy said, was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his military was losing ground in a key frontline region and sustaining higher levels of casualties. The Kremlin was not available to comment on Saturday. But in a statement [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"urging foreign nationals to leave Kyiv"], the Russian Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians. COUNTEROFFENSIVE IN DONBAS Zelenskiy said a successful Ukrainian counteroffensive, code-named "Vivaldi", had recaptured around 140 sq km (54 sq miles) of Ukrain's eastern Donbas region and was still ongoing. Russia has said it must control Donbas in its entirety as a condition for any peace deal. In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump's administration has sought to revive talks to end the four-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two. The US leader last month urged Ukraine [USN:L1N45503J TEXT:"to refrain from hitting Russian oil installations"], saying that was sending global diesel prices surging. But Zelenskiy, speaking as air raid sirens blared outside the gilded halls of the presidential offices, said he had received no indications from Russia that Putin was interested in peace talks, or discussing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure. Over the past week, the Ukrainian capital has come under persistent attack by Russian drones and missiles targeting energy and telecoms assets, road and rail infrastructure. For the first time, Russia has [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"targeted the bridges"] across the Dnipro river connecting east and west Kyiv. Zelenskiy said Ukraine would react to the change in tactics by Moscow, but would not target civilian infrastructure indiscriminately. "We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war," Zelenskiy said in English. "But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects." SUPPORT FROM EUROPE After the Trump administration invited Putin [USN:L6N45F16H TEXT:"to attend a G20 summit in Miami"] in December and discussed business deals with Russian envoys, Zelenskiy urged Washington not to normalise relations with Russia before ensuring a return to peace. Zelenskiy said he would be happy to meet Putin for peace talks at the G20, but he warned the US not to believe in "illusions" that Russia would simply end hostilities if it gained control of Donbas. "It's not fair just to normalise," said Zelenskiy, dressed in his trademark black T-shirt and military-style jacket. Any resumption of economic and diplomatic ties with the West had to be in return for Russia ending hostilities, he said: "Because peace is more important than any kind of economy." While the US has proposed a resumption of trilateral talks in the coming weeks in the UAE, Zelenskiy noted that an exact date and location for the technical-level conversations had still not been set. Ukrainian officials warn that Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of an expected winter onslaught against electricity and water infrastructure. Last winter, the worst of the war, Russian strikes left swathes of the country without electricity and heating for days at a time. Since the summer, Moscow has also begun launching dozens of fast and relatively cheap jet-powered Shahed drones a day at Ukraine, whose air defence teams have struggled to cope because their interceptor drones were too slow to catch them. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had been forced to rely heavily on its fighter aircraft – F-16s and MiGs – to down around 60% of the Russian jet-powered drones, but supplies of 20 mm ammunition for the planes were running low. Kyiv was urgently working on other solutions – including boosting its electronic jamming capabilities, he said. In the second half of October, it would receive the first shipment of small, cheap air defence missiles capable of hitting the new Shaheds. Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was developing five models of new interceptor drones capable of downing the jet Shaheds. Fresh from a meeting with his defence chiefs, he said tests on two of those models showed a modest success rate of around 30%. "We'll have to scale it," he said. "I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way." BALLISTIC THREAT Ukraine announced the first combat use this week of its own domestically made ballistic missile, the FP-7, which has a range of around 250 km (155 miles). Zelenskiy said he had called the manufacturer Fire Point to pressure executives to finish a longer-range model, the FP-9, which the company has said could hit Moscow. "I said to them, where is my FP-9?" said Zelenskiy, with a grin. "We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be (ready) this autumn, I'm sure." Zelenskiy said a recent spate of Russian drone incursions and hybrid attacks in Europe were an effort to intimidate European populations and to undermine support for Ukraine. Some European leaders were starting to understand this, he said, and toughen their position. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. After talks with European officials in Brussels this week, Ukraine had unlocked funding to order the drones that it needs to keep fighting at the start of 2027, Zelenskiy said. Ukrainian officials had worked on plans with European partners to plug a $27 billion hole in Kyiv's defence budget this year. The plans involve a combination of the reallocation of Ukraine's own budget resources, bilateral assistance and using "money credits" from next year's portion of a €90 billion EU loan, Zelenskiy said. "We will close this (gap). I think this is absolutely a big success for our country," he said.

item.title: US Coast Guard finds debris from missing medical aircraft off Nantucket
item.description: The US Coast Guard said late on Saturday it found debris from a medical transport aircraft off the shore of Massachusetts' Nantucket island and was searching for six people who were on board.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang, Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: The US Coast Guard said late on Saturday it found debris from a medical transport aircraft off the shore of Massachusetts' Nantucket island and was searching for six people who were on board. The Federal Aviation Administration told the Coast Guard early on Saturday that it had lost contact with a Gulfstream jet traveling from Bermuda to Boston. Several hours later, the Coast Guard said in a statement that it "located a debris field that has been confirmed to be associated with the missing aircraft." Four Canadians were on the plane, Canadian Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon said on X. "We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue efforts continue," he wrote. The other two passengers were Bermudian nationals, the Coast Guard said. Searches will continue throughout the night near Nantucket, an island community south of mainland Massachusetts, they said. The aircraft, registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, departed Bermuda at 12:41 a.m. on Saturday (0301 GMT), according to data from flight tracking website FlightAware. The plane was flying at 24,000 feet (7,300 metres) for much of the flight before descending 13,000 feet in about two minutes shortly before flight controllers lost contact, data showed. Local TV station Boston 25 posted an audio clip from Boston Logan International Airport in which an air traffic controller can be heard asking the Gulfstream pilot, "You said you're coming in blind? Is that what you said?" The controller then asked whether the plane was declaring an emergency. No response was heard. Latitude is based in Ontario, Canada, and provides medical evacuation services. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Bermuda government is in contact with US authorities and the families of the passengers, Bermuda Premier David Burt wrote in a statement posted on Instagram. "We are praying that all six people will be found safe," he wrote.

Two Iranians appear in UK court over alleged plot to target Jews

FAST

LONDON: Two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court on Saturday (Oct 3) charged with plotting acts of terrorism involving the use of a homemade bomb to attack the Jewish community in northern England at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran. Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were arrested on Sep 20 at the start of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, when they are accused of carrying out "hostile" surveillance on potential Jewish targets in Manchester, prosecutors say. These targets included the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park synagogue, the scene of a deadly attack almost a year ago in which two Jewish worshippers were killed, prosecutor Mark Luckett told Westminster Magistrates' Court. ALLEGED PLOT INVOLVED HOMEMADE DEVICE "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device," Luckett said.

He said the men were accused of being in contact with a third party who is alleged to have directed and coordinated the attack planning and provided instructions on how to assemble a homemade device, which prosecutors allege would have been made from chlorine and brake fluid. "It's assessed that this individual is also an Iranian national and most likely operating from within Iran," Luckett said.

Related:

UK's Starmer convenes community leaders to fight antisemitism after attacks

Two Jewish men stabbed in London, police treat attack as terrorism

The court was told both men had come to Britain from Europe in small boats. Salehi had arrived in 2020 and had been granted asylum, while Ahmadyan came in 2023 and his asylum claim was still outstanding, Luckett said. The men did not enter a plea and were remanded in custody until their next hearing at London's Old Bailey court on Oct 23. The case comes a week after Britain said Iran was believed to be involved in a suspected plot to target the RAF Fairford air base which the US military has used to carry out raids against targets in Iran, leading to a dual British-Iranian national being arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. Police said on Saturday he had been released on police bail while the investigation continues. British counterterrorism police have said the Manchester allegations were not connected in any way to the Fairford investigation. Iran has rejected accusations of involvement in a number of plots in Britain in recent years, and said allegations it was connected to the Fairford incident were baseless. Britain has also seen a significant rise in antisemitism since the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023 that triggered the subsequent war in Gaza, including a series of attacks on Jewish sites in London earlier this year. "It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime," Home Secretary (interior minister) Shabana Mahmood said in a statement. "They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement."

Source: Reuters/ec

item.description: Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Saturday they had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen's Sanaa and other provinces. A large plume of smoke and fire was seen rising in the vicinity of an Aramco facility in Riyadh earlier on Saturday, a witness told Reuters. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of an attack on an Aramco facility. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The reported attack comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure. The Houthis said last week they had attacked Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu with missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia said at the time that it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards Taif and the Yanbu area, but did not report damage to Aramco facilities.

item.title: In crude Ohio rally speech, Trump says he may not help if Democrats win
item.description: "Just get out and vote," Trump said at a rally for Republican candidates. "If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big, and we're going to shove it up their ass."
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump used an Ohio rally on Saturday to mix profane attacks on Democrats with promises of financial help if Republicans win the midterms and a warning that he would be less willing to work with the state if Democrats prevail. "Just get out and vote," Trump said at a rally for Republican candidates, including US Senator Jon Husted and Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. "If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big, and we're going to shove it up their ass." Multiple incumbent Republican senators across the country face tough political headwinds in the November 3 elections, with Trump's [USN:L6N45D0XN TEXT:"popularity falling"] in recent months as higher prices persist for gasoline and other staples amid the US-Israeli war with Iran. Both Husted and Ramaswamy are in competitive races against Democratic opponents. Former US Senator Sherrod Brown is running against Husted. Amy Acton is facing Ramaswamy. OHIO A KEY STATE IN MIDTERMS Polls have suggested that Democrats could gain ground in the midterms, which will decide control of the narrowly divided House of Representatives and Senate, but Trump said Republicans would do better than critics expect. "I think we're going to have a big surprise because they don't know what's happening," he told the crowd in Vandalia, Ohio. Ohio's is among eight US Senate races rated competitive. The state has turned into a campaign battlefield over [USN:L6N45916H TEXT:"data centers"] and culture war issues such as youth transgender surgeries. Trump repeatedly attacked Democrats during his speech, at one point calling them "dumb son of a bitches," while arguing that maintaining Republican control would give Ohio officials a direct line to his administration and make it easier for the state to secure federal help. He said Ohio's elected Republican officials frequently call him seeking money for the state, adding that he would be less inclined to accommodate Democrats if they win key races. Referring to Acton, Trump said: "But I'm not going to help her." Husted is counting on Trump to motivate supporters who might otherwise skip the midterms, but the senator also directly criticized Brown, a veteran Democrat, as someone who has accomplished little in his political career. "He's been in office for 50 years — can you name one thing that he has done for you?" Husted said at the rally. A spokesperson for Brown's campaign criticized Husted for backing Trump's policy on Iran and said Husted supported "sweetheart tax deals" that lured data centers to Ohio. "Jon Husted puts corporations and billionaires first every time, and we all pay for it," Brown spokesperson Lauren Chou said in an email to Reuters. Trump garnered more than 55% of the Ohio vote in the 2024 presidential election, but economic concerns since then have sunk his approval ratings. Ohio gasoline prices increased 35% over the past year to $4.16 per gallon on average, according to AAA, which compiles data on automobile travel. Trump's trade policy with Canada has led to retaliatory Canadian tariffs that affect about $3 billion worth of Ohio exports, based on 2025 figures, according to a CBC report. DEBATE ON DATA CENTERS Talking to reporters shortly before addressing Saturday's rally, Husted said the US has to win the Iran war "on our terms" and in the interim, he is "showing people that I'm fighting for lower prices." He spoke to a sympathetic crowd at the rally, but he also needs to sell his message to people like independent voter Jonathan Smith. Smith, a 19-year-old construction worker, held a sign reading, "Where are my lower gas prices?" outside his former high school in Vandalia, north of Dayton. "I've got a wedding to save up for, and with gas prices continuously going up, it's getting harder and harder to put aside money," said Smith, adding he is still deciding whom to vote for in the Senate race. Outside political groups have poured [USN:L6N458188 TEXT:"tens of millions"] of dollars into Ohio, making Husted-Brown the second-most-expensive Senate race in the country, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Rallygoers shared mixed opinions on the hot-button issue of data centers in the state. "I'm not huge on the AI data centers," Samuel Clevenger, 20, said when discussing Husted's candidacy. But the apprentice plumber said he was encouraged to vote by Trump's attention to the state, as well as his 2025 policy capping taxes on overtime. On the other side of the rally venue, Brenda White, 60, held a sign encouraging building in her northeastern Ohio town: "DATA CENTER SOUTH LORAIN." As Husted met voters in the bleachers, she urged the senator to support the center's construction in place of a steel mill. "You want a data center there?" Husted asked. Before White posed for her photo with Husted, a man in the senator's entourage asked: "Can we do it without the sign?"

item.title: New term gives US Supreme Court's Thomas and Alito more chances to wield power
item.description: The two oldest and most conservative justices are at the height of their influence.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The new US Supreme Court term that begins on Monday presents opportunities for its two eldest and most conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, to help push US law further rightward on contentious issues such as gun rights, religion in public schools and voting restrictions. Thomas, 78, has served on the top US judicial body since 1991, making him the [USN:L1N41E02Q TEXT:"second-longest-serving justice"] in American history. Alito, 76, has served since 2006. Earlier in their tenures, they often found themselves in dissent in major decisions, but the court, with a 6-3 conservative majority since 2020, has shifted dramatically to the right. Thomas and Alito now are perhaps at the height of their influence and have been lavished with praise by Republican President Donald Trump . 'WHY LEAVE?' If either were to retire, that would clear the way for Trump to nominate a younger conservative replacement who could serve for decades in the lifetime position. But, at least for now, according to legal experts, they appear more interested in wielding that power than stepping aside. "They have been waiting for a long time to be in the position," political science professor Kevin McMahon of Trinity College in Connecticut said of Thomas and Alito. "So why leave?" During the court's term that ended in June, Thomas and Alito helped deliver long-sought victories to the conservative legal movement. These included a [USN:S0N3YR013 TEXT:"ruling"] expanding presidential control over regulatory agencies, and a [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"decision"] further limiting the scope of the Voting Rights Act, the landmark 1965 law intended to eliminate racial discrimination in voting. Thomas and Alito have been Trump's most reliable votes in cases involving his extraordinary exertion of presidential powers. [USN:L1N45H0WL TEXT:"More such cases are coming"] during the new nine-month term, including two involving Trump's hardline [USN:S0N43101E TEXT:"immigration policies"]. The court's docket also includes November 3 arguments in a [USN:L1N4130K0 TEXT:"challenge"] to a Colorado law requiring preschools receiving taxpayer money to enroll children of same-sex couples, the latest clash between religious rights and LGBT protections to reach the justices. The justices also may take up a case examining whether a Texas law that requires public elementary and high schools to display the [USN:L1N45G0IM TEXT:"biblical Ten Commandments"] in classrooms comports with the US Constitution's prohibition on the government establishing or endorsing any particular religion or promoting religion over nonreligion. On December 2, the court will [USN:S0N3YR01V TEXT:"hear"] arguments over whether states can ban AR-15s and other semiautomatic rifles, an opportunity for the conservative justices to further expand gun rights. Thomas and Alito have been instrumental in major guns rulings since 2008. On December 8, the court will [USN:S0N41Y01G TEXT:"consider"] whether Arizona can mandate that people registering to vote provide proof of citizenship, a Republican-backed measure critics have called an effort to make it harder for groups who tend to support Democratic candidates to register. Legal experts said these cases give Thomas and Alito chances to build on some of their most influential earlier rulings and target more Supreme Court precedents they consider misguided. "They have more they want to accomplish, and I expect them to keep pushing on a host of issues," McMahon said, adding that they even may envision themselves serving as a check on a potential future Democratic president beginning in 2029. "They're still in their seventies," McMahon said. "And for a Supreme Court justice, it's not unprecedented that you stay on the bench well into your eighties." 'LEGENDS, BOTH' Thomas and Alito backed every major Trump administration policy that came before the court last term, unlike the three conservative justices Trump appointed during his first term — Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett. Those three all have compiled very conservative records as justices but in a few major cases sided against Trump. Trump [USN:L6N45N0QS TEXT:"told"] Time magazine this week he regretted nominating all three, calling them disloyal. "I gave them the position of a lifetime, and they vote against me often," Trump said. Thomas and Alito, on the other hand, are "[USN:FWN4570D3 TEXT:"legends, both"]," Trump said last month after they dissented from a decision that blocked his plans to restrict mail-in voting. "Alito and Thomas are the two who have figured out how to never get into Trump's doghouse," University of Minnesota political science professor Timothy Johnson said. Alito rejected the notion that he is a rubber stamp for Trump and his administration, telling the Wall Street Journal in August: "I vote in every case the way I think the case should be decided. If that means a high correlation with what Trump wants, fine. If it means zero correlation with what Trump wants, fine as well." 'A VALUABLE CONTRIBUTION' Speculation among court watchers about a possible vacancy has ramped up as the two men draw closer to the average age of retirement for Supreme Court justices since 2000 — about 80 years old — and with the November 3 US congressional elections looming. If Democrats take control of the Senate, they could try to block Trump's nominee to fill any vacancy created by the retirement or death of a sitting justice. Alito tamped down retirement speculation for now, telling the Wall Street Journal: "Obviously, I'm here for another term." The term runs through the end of June. In a CBS News interview excerpt released on Friday, Alito said he thought about retiring this year, calling retirement something someone his age must think about every year. "But I thought that I could still make a valuable contribution, which is why I became a justice and a judge in the first place," Alito said. "It's too hard to predict, for anybody, particularly when you reach a certain age, what your situation will be a year from now, two years from now, and so forth," Alito said. "And it's too hard to predict what the political situation will be, and what any president might do with respect to a replacement." ABORTION RIGHTS Alito has a lot of influence in conversations among the court's conservatives, said Peter Canellos, author of a recent Alito biography titled "Revenge for the Sixties." "A lot of the action on the Supreme Court right now is conservative on conservative," Canellos said. "It's entirely a discussion among conservatives." Canellos said Alito's influence was highlighted by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, perhaps the most important ruling he has authored. It overturned the 1973 Roe v. Wade precedent that had recognized a woman's constitutional right to have an abortion. Chief Justice John Roberts, a stalwart conservative, dissented from the portion of Alito's ruling that reversed Roe. "I think over the years Alito has thought of himself as an instrumental justice," Canellos said. "You can see in many cases, Dobbs included, that his key ability is to bring the three Trump appointees to his side, rather than Chief Justice Roberts' side, when the two of them disagree." In Dobbs, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh and Barrett joined Alito. "I suspect that Alito felt that even if he were replaced by a true conservative, which was the core of the argument why he should resign, it was not in any way preordained that that person would have the kind of influence that he has," Canellos added. Alito has long criticized a 1990 Supreme Court precedent that limits the ability of people to seek religious exemptions from generally applicable laws. Religious rights advocates have said that ruling infringes on First Amendment protections for free exercise of religion. The 1990 ruling specifically held that the First Amendment does not protect people who participate in illegal acts — in that case, the use of an illegal hallucinogenic drug — as part of a religious ceremony. The religious freedom case being argued in November, called St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, gives Alito and the other conservative justices a chance to cast doubt on the 1990 precedent, known as Employment Division v. Smith. 'WHY NOT CONTINUE?' The case involving state-level bans on assault-style rifles may give Thomas a chance to clarify a test he laid out in one of his most impactful rulings, a 2022 case called New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen. Under this test, gun control measures must be "consistent with this nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation" — not simply advance an important government interest — in order to comply with the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms. Some judges have said this wording does not provide clear guidance, producing inconsistent results. "He has clearly expressed frustration that his colleagues have dodged reviews of assault-weapon prohibitions, making these consolidated challenges from Connecticut and Illinois a long-sought vehicle to establish a nationwide constitutional rule that includes these specific guns," Johnson said of Thomas. Thomas has not addressed retirement rumors, but in the past has hinted at a lengthy tenure. McMahon said Thomas may want to become the longest-serving justice, a milestone he would reach in May 2028. "If you're that close, and you have the setup that he has, why not continue?" McMahon asked.

As public fears of AI grow, Trump digs in on voluntary safeguards

US House Speaker Mike Johnson, US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, and OpenAI President Greg Brockman attend a luncheon for tech leaders hosted by US President Donald Trump in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., US, September 29, 2026. WASHINGTON, Oct 3 : US President Donald Trump spent Tuesday showcasing his administration’s approach to AI — touting the US government’s new AI chatbot, dining with tech titans at the White House, and announcing a voluntary agreement with those executives that he said would address growing fears about the technology's safety. The display signaled that Trump is eager to show he is addressing growing voter concerns about AI's dangers without imposing restrictions that could hamper the technology's development, AI safety advocates said. The safety agreement with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Trump described it as “morally binding.” “This was an attempt to give the impression that the government is listening to these concerns without undercutting what has been a very clear and consistent line from this administration: that regulation and governance inherently impede innovation,” said Kat Duffy, who runs an AI team at the nonpartisan Council on Foreign Relations. Whether voters buy Trump's effort in the run-up to US midterm elections on November 3 remains to be seen. Public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months. Three-quarters of Americans worry that AI companies have not gone far enough to prevent AI from causing serious harm to society, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published September 22. A series of security events has also underscored how advanced AI can act unpredictably.

Hundreds of OpenAI AI agents broke out of their testing environment in July and attacked the infrastructure of AI platform Hugging Face. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, saying that the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade." His words, and others, sparked a flurry of calls from US lawmakers for AI regulation.  Through it all, Trump has largely dismissed those concerns, saying that government restrictions would make it harder for American companies to compete against their Chinese counterparts. He has repeatedly said that US law enforcement agencies such as the Justice Department serve as sufficient guardrails, and that no new rules are needed. He also directed his administration to call AI "super intelligence," part of an effort to improve the reputation of an unpopular technology.  The concerns have become prominent enough to make their way into late-night comedy. In late September, "Saturday Night Live" satirized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, one of the industry's most outspoken voices on AI risks — even as his company readies a public stock sale that could value it at $2 trillion — with cast member Jane Wickline portraying the executive. "AI is not a weapon, it’s a tool: A tool for building weapons. And I urge you to urge me to stop," Wickline said as Amodei. CONCERNS ABOUT ENFORCEMENT The accord, inked Tuesday, does include measures that AI safety advocates have sought, including calling for “robust internal controls” to prevent unauthorized hacks as well as partnering with “independent external auditors.” Those concepts have been included in draft state and federal legislation, and California in September enacted the first state law setting rules for how independent auditors evaluate AI products. But the one-page White House document did not address details or enforcement mechanisms. A White House official said in a statement that the agreement will "advance American innovation and strengthen responsible development" of AI models. Trump is expected to name his Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as his top AI adviser, Reuters previously reported, a position he has dubbed "AI czar," even as Clayton stays in his role leading the nation's intelligence agencies. Representative Ro Khanna, a Democrat representing Silicon Valley, welcomed the idea of "independent auditors" but said that they should report to an independent federal agency. "They can’t just be auditors that report to (OpenAI CEO) Sam Altman or Dario Amodei," he said. "My concern is the president basically trusting these guys who have a huge profit motive and won’t have the judgment to keep us safe." Venture capitalist David Sacks, who advises Trump on AI and has been an advocate for unrestricted AI development, said on the social media platform X that securities law and other legal authorities would penalize companies that fail to address problems uncovered by internal controls or auditors. But AI safety advocates told Reuters those authorities can only address harms after they occur, saying the threats require safeguards designed to prevent large-scale harm before it happens. Nevertheless, some AI observers saw the simple fact of hosting the event as an indication that Trump is absorbing the worries. Trump’s agreement with the tech executives is “a shift toward acknowledging that there are serious safety and security concerns that merit closer coordination between the companies,” said Samuel Hammond, AI policy director at the conservative Foundation for American Innovation.

Source: Reuters

MANILA: The Philippines, chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), expressed concern over an airstrike in Myanmar's Rakhine state that caused deaths, injuries and destruction, and stood ready to facilitate discussions within the regional bloc on how best to assist Myanmar. "The Philippines is closely monitoring developments and expresses concern over the attacks which resulted in destruction, loss of lives and injuries to those affected," Foreign Affairs Assistant Secretary for ASEAN Affairs Ana Marie Hernando said in an email response on Saturday (Oct 3). As ASEAN chair, Manila said it remained mindful of the views of all member states and would continue to be guided by the regional bloc's consensus-based approach. The Philippines said it stood ready to facilitate discussions within ASEAN on ways to assist Myanmar, in line with the common aspiration of finding a solution that is "Myanmar-owned and led". Monday's Kyauktaw airstrike, Rakhine's deadliest such attack since a December hospital bombing, killed 50 people and wounded dozens more. Myanmar has been locked in a nationwide civil war since a 2021 coup, with an alliance of armed groups, including the Arakan Army, fighting against the military. The protracted conflict has since killed around 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million in the impoverished Southeast Asian nation.

Source: Reuters/js

item.title: High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement
item.description: While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement

While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade.

Police officers stand in front of protestors amid tear gas as protesting students carry out blockading action near the Kerichen high school in Brest, western France, on Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Fred Tanneau)

03 Oct 2026 03:36PM (Updated: 03 Oct 2026 03:42PM)

AUBERVILLIERS: Maisa, a 17-year-old in a poor Paris suburb who aspires to be an English teacher, joined tens of thousands of other students and their supporters this week in protests that spread across France over dilapidated schools, classroom overcrowding and teacher shortages.  At Lycee Le Corbusier school in Aubervilliers, a suburb north of Paris in the Seine-Saint-Denis department, protesters said schools in poor neighbourhoods like theirs faced the worst conditions. “Last year I took the high school French exam without a French teacher, and teachers have a huge impact,” Maisa said. "These are not conditions to study in."

As protests raged at more than 1,200 French high schools this week, police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets in some cases. More than 5,000 people were arrested, and some protesters were seriously hurt with eye injuries, broken teeth and blows to the head. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it a "climate of unacceptable violence" and called for order. Amelia, 15, joined Maisa in the crowd outside the school gates and held a sign reading, "Our address should not decide our future". She said she was demonstrating to demand the same rights as students elsewhere in the country.       "The education authority is not investing enough in the suburbs. It's classist and racist," she said.  Ulysse Rabate, a political scientist at Paris 8 University, said the protests show the way that France's marginalised urban neighbourhoods are increasingly influencing national politics. "When there is a collapse of the public service, of public education, those who feel it the most, and the most violently, are those at bottom," he said.

A French firefighter extinguishes a fire on the street amid clashes between protesters and police during a high school students protest in Pantin near Paris as part of nationwide protests to demand the hiring of substitute teachers, increased resources and better learning conditions, as more than 400 schools remain closed following days of student protests that have escalated into violence in some places, France, Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Tom Nicholson)

POLITICAL FLASHPOINT The nationwide demonstrations and blockades , which began last week, have become a political flashpoint at a sensitive moment for the government, which announced a series of deeply unpopular spending cuts in its 2027 budget on Thursday. The education budget is set to increase by a below-inflation 1.7 per cent to €65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions. The education ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said that education remained a priority and the below-inflation budget increase was due to population decline. The protests started in the Parisian suburbs, where poverty levels are high, then spread to Paris itself and other French towns, including Marseille, Strasbourg, Tours and Lille.  At Lycee Le Corbusier, classes including maths, humanities, English and sport have been canceled since the start of the academic year due to a teacher shortage, according to Karima Kara Ali, an elected parent representative.  In Seine-Saint-Denis, two-thirds of high schools took part in protests on Thursday, the CGT labour union said. Youth, teachers and parents in four towns complained of unsanitary school conditions and chronic staff shortages including of nurses and social workers.  Louise Paternoster, a representative for the Seine-Saint-Denis branch of the CGT's education union, said the area does not get adequate resources for its student population and their educational needs. Two-thirds of schools in the department have unfilled teacher positions, according to a union survey.

A student carries a barrier in front of a banner which reads "equal opportunities" suspended on the front of Louis-le-Grand high school in central Paris, on Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Simon Wohlfahrt)

NOT ENOUGH TEACHERS "Our students are losing out on study time. Some schools don't have drinking water. We are not equal to other departments," she said, blaming shortages on government cuts of 3,256 teacher positions nationwide in 2026. In Pantin, a town on the northeastern edge of Paris, teacher Dilan Roche joined her students as they protested outside their school this week to support their demands and protect them from the police. "What they wrote on banners, we wrote in a letter to the local education authority: overcrowded classes, no nurses, no social workers - which is problematic for students with learning difficulties, many living in precarity," she said. While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade, standing at €11,660 in 2024 and €11,910 in 2010, according to education ministry data.  The last nationwide high school protest movement on this scale demanding more funding came in the 1990s. That followed the government sharply expanding access to the baccalauréat, the school-leaving exam that typically paves the way to university, without providing schools with sufficient additional resources, said Professor Clemence Cardon-Quint at Paul Valery University, who researches education funding.  The movement won an increase in funding, but spending per student later stagnated despite growing demands on schools. Cardon-Quint said students and teachers have taken on additional responsibilities over the years, including navigating Parcoursup, the university admissions system introduced in 2018 and criticised by some students and teachers as opaque and discriminatory. "In a period of budgetary restraint, it is more difficult to reduce inequalities," said Cardon-Quint.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ドバイ／エルサレム　３日　ロイター］ - アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のドバイからイスラエルのテルアビブに向かっていたＵＡＥの格安航空（ＬＣＣ）フライドバイ機内で副操縦士が機長を刺した事件で、ＵＡＥの検事総長は３日、副操縦士が飛行中に「テロ」攻撃を実行しようとしたと述べた。国営通信ＷＡＭが伝えた。

ハマド・サイフ・アル・シャムシ検事総長は「フライドバイＦＺ１０７３便を巡る事件の捜査で、副操縦士がテロ攻撃を企てていたことが判明した」と述べた。

副操縦士は操縦室内に備え付けられている非常時用のおの（クラッシュアックス） で機長を襲い、機長に代わって操縦しようとしたという。検事総長は、容疑者の動機を含めＦＺ１０７３便を巡る捜査は続いており、「必要な手続き」が済み次第、結果を公表すると述べた。

ＵＡＥ大統領の上級顧問を務めるアンワル・ガルガシュ氏は、ＵＡＥはテロを一切容認せず、過激主義的な言説にも寛容な姿勢は取らないとＸに投稿した。

ＵＡＥ当局は副操縦士の身元を公表していないが、関係者は、オマーン国籍のハマム・アルハマミ容疑者だと述べた。捜査について説明を受けた別の関係筋も、その名前を確認した。ＵＡＥ当局は、容疑者の身元に関するロイターの問い合わせに返答していない。

フライドバイの広報担当者は、事件の詳しい状況は引き続き調査中で、これ以上のコメントはできないと述べた。

＜イスラエル、捜査に参加の意向、オマーンは沈黙＞

副操縦士は、同機が緊急着陸したサウジアラビアで身柄を拘束された。サウジ内務省によると、機長とともに１日朝にサウジからアブダビに向かった。

同機の搭乗客は大半がイスラエル人だった。イスラエル政府当局者は２日、ＵＡＥ主導の捜査に加わり、何が起きたのかを解明し、容疑者の動機や経歴を調べるとロイターに語った。捜査について説明を受けた関係筋は２日、イスラエルの当局者がＵＡＥで副操縦士を事情聴取する見通しだと述べた。どの機関や当局が聴取するかは明らかにしなかった。

副操縦士について、イスラエル側は早い段階からオマーン国籍だと指摘していた。イスラエルとオマーンの間に正式な外交関係はなく、イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相は、そうした国の操縦士がイスラエル便を運航することは認められていないと述べている。副操縦士がテルアビブ便の乗務に就いた経緯は分かっていない。オマーンは事件についてコメントしていない。

item.title: 独経済、今年1％前後成長も 財政支出と輸出寄与と連銀総裁
item.description: ［フランクフルト ２日 ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独経済、今年1％前後成長も　財政支出と輸出寄与と連銀総裁 10/3 15:46 配信

2023年11月、キプロス中央銀行で開催された会合で撮影　REUTERS/Yiannis Kourtoglou

［フランクフルト　２日　ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後になる可能性があると述べた。堅調な輸出需要と政府投資が寄与する。同中銀が６月に示した予測（０．５％）の２倍となる。

ドイツは過去３年間ほとんど成長していない。イラン戦争に起因するエネルギー価格高騰が産業に打撃を与えている。

ナーゲル氏は講演で、生産は予想外に底堅いと指摘した。潜在成長率は依然として低いものの、ドイツは景気循環上の回復局面にあるとの認識を示した。

「年平均で１％前後の実質経済成長となる可能性は十分にある」と述べ、「３年間の停滞を経て、これは確かに小さいながらも歓迎すべき兆しとなるだろう」とした。

ナーゲル氏は、連邦政府の国防やインフラなどに重点を置いた財政支出を成長けん引役の一つとし、予想外に堅調な海外需要の恩恵も受けているとした。

ドイツの主要経済研究所も先月下旬に、今年と来年の経済成長率予測を上方修正した。今年の成長率予測は０．６％から１．３％に引き上げられた。

item.title: トランプ氏、公的医療保険加入者に90ドル給付表明 2000万人超
item.description:
Kanishka Singh
［ワシントン ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kanishka Singh

［ワシントン　２日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は、高齢者向け公的医療保険「メディケア」に加入する米国民２０００万人超に対し、毎月の保険料負担を軽減するため、１人当たり９０ドルを一時金として支給すると表明した。

トランプ氏は２日深夜、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）への投稿で、給付金は「メディケア改善基金」から拠出すると説明。同基金には、メディケアの出来高払い制度の改善を目的として議会から２０億ドルが拠出されているとした。

ホワイトハウスのウェブサイトによると、対象の高齢者の大半に１０月上旬に９０ドルが銀行口座に直接振り込まれる。口座振り込みを利用していない対象者には、メディケアに登録した住所に小切手を送付する。発送も１０月上旬になるという。

トランプ氏は１１月の中間選挙を前に、有権者にばらまき的施策を打ち出している。９月には、中間選挙で勝利すれば成人に５０００ドルの「トランプ配当」を給付すると提案した。

政権は、１００万人近い米国民への５００ドルの給付も進めている。ホワイトハウスは、この５００ドルの給付について、医療保険制度改革法（ＡＣＡ）に基づく保険の加入者から過剰に徴収されたとする保険料の払い戻しだと説明している。給付は全米を対象としたものでなく、連邦政府の医療保険加入サイトを利用する３０州の一部住民に限られる。対象州には主要な激戦州が多く含まれ、選挙戦略の専門家らは、一部の選挙戦の結果に影響を及ぼす可能性があると指摘している。

item.title: ゴルフ＝畑岡と山下が7位、首位と3打差 ロッテ選手権
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのロッテ選手権は２日、米ハワイ州エワビーチのホアカレイＣＣ（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、前日３６位の畑岡奈紗が７バーディー、ノーボギーの６５をマークし、通算９アンダーの１３５で７位に浮上した。

１０位で出た山下美夢有も８バーディー、３ボギーの６７で回り、通算９アンダーで畑岡と並ぶ７位。首位とは３打差につけた。

岩井明愛は６９で回り、通算７アンダーの１３７で１４位。西郷真央は７０で通算６アンダーの１３８とし、２２位に後退した。

岩井千怜、竹田麗央、笹生優花は３３位。吉田優利は４５位、櫻井心那と西村優菜は５７位で、そのほかの日本選手は予選落ちとなった。

上位では、ポリー・マック（ドイツ）とジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）がともに６５をマークし、通算１２アンダーの１３２で首位。１打差の１１アンダーにカロリナ・メルグラティ（イタリア）とユン・イナ（韓国）が続いた。

item.title: Analysis:AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out
item.description: LONDON, Oct 3 : Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital.Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Analysis:AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out

FILE PHOTO: "AI Artificial Intelligence" words, a keyboard and a robotics hand in this illustration taken, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

FAST

LONDON, Oct 3 : Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital. Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC, almost matching the value of outstanding US Treasuries. It "dwarfs" what was spent in the railroad or dotcom booms, even after adjusting for inflation, PwC said. Meanwhile, Anthropic, just one of the major firms in the AI race, plans to spend $518 billion in coming years, according to the IPO prospectus seen by Reuters, which is more than 100 times its 2025 revenue. Its backers say AI technology will be more transformational than the advent of steam engines and the industrialization they powered. Yet lurking behind the dizzying projections and huge outlays by AI companies, alongside sky-high valuations, lie assumptions about vast broad-based productivity gains and future profits with little evidence so far - or historical precedent - to be sure they can deliver, economists say.

PRODUCTIVITY GAINS 'REMAIN ELUSIVE' JP Morgan wrote in August that broad-based productivity gains in the US, which leads the AI race, "remain elusive", raising questions about the sustainability of AI valuations. A Bain & Company study said productivity gains from existing markets would not be enough to justify current outlays and "entirely new markets must emerge to close the funding gap", suggesting those could range from using AI-guided robots to developing new materials for batteries and semiconductors. US hyperscalers - the companies rolling out infrastructure around the world like Google, Amazon and Microsoft - and others in the AI race needed to find more than $4.2 trillion of new revenue in the next five years to fund the buildout, Bain said. "The question is whether the applications arrive in time to pay for it," according to the study, published last month. Few doubt the potential of AI to transform everything from work in an office to research labs, just as past revolutions shrank journey times from days to hours or connected the world at the touch of a keyboard. What seems more immutable is the maths behind securing a return on investment or the deadlines for repaying loans, leaving economists to work out the implications for the global economy beyond the ups and downs of investment cycles. "Historical precedent suggests that technology-driven booms often end when infrastructure buildouts cease to deliver sufficient returns," JP Morgan wrote. Using the example of Nvidia, the US company whose chips are the backbone of the AI revolution, JP Morgan estimated US productivity gains would need to be 3 per cent to 5 per cent annually over the next 10 years to justify its valuation. That would be a substantial increase from the baseline expectation of the US Congressional Budget Office of 1.75 per cent annual productivity growth for that period. For the US alone - which according to some estimates accounts for about three quarters of the global AI investment total - investment will run as high as about $9 trillion from 2025 to 2032, equivalent to spending 3.2 per cent of US GDP each year, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. He estimates the US AI sector would need to generate about $3.55 trillion in annual revenue by 2032 to earn a 10 per cent return on investment. It earns a fraction of that now. The leveraged structure of much of the debt funding AI infrastructure also means "a relatively modest deterioration in demand, delays, or asset values can therefore produce much larger losses," he wrote in a conference paper, revised in October. AI AND 'THE RATE OF NEW WONDERS' The dizzying numbers have not stopped US AI bosses speaking with an otherworldly zeal about changes afoot. Anthropic's Dario Amodei has said an AI future could be "a thing of transcendent beauty", while OpenAI's Sam Altman has said "the rate of new wonders being achieved will be immense" as models learn to improve themselves and accelerate breakthroughs. Jasjeet Sekhon, chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind, told a summit at UC Berkeley in August that this self-teaching, known as recursive self-improvement, was a "key part of the investment thesis", and that it could, if achieved, deliver unprecedented productivity gains. Recursive self-improvement, while potentially delivering exponential AI advances, has also raised concerns about existential risks to humanity. Yet the pace of change in productivity might still end up lagging the timelines needed by corporate accounts departments. Diane Coyle, an economist at Britain's Cambridge University, said the productivity impact of past revolutionary technologies had usually taken about 10 to 50 years to feed through. Anthropic's economics team modeled a range of scenarios for how much extra growth AI would deliver at an annual rate in 2030. Assuming a baseline of 2 per cent in a non-AI environment, it suggested growth of 2.4 per cent in a scenario with modest AI impact, 5.4 per cent in a substantial scenario and 15.4 per cent in an extreme scenario. Higher growth would mean more jobs lost, it said, without assigning probabilities for any of the outcomes. Amodei forecast last year that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. For now, however, some researchers say it appears to have been limited to making it harder for those seeking office work to find a job. Studies in the US and Britain have pointed to a slowdown in early career hiring for white-collar positions performing tasks at which AI is adept, even if overall employment remains strong. Researchers at Stanford University said in August that employment of workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed industries, such as accountants and paralegals, was 19 per cent lower than for jobs that AI found hard to replicate, like janitors and builders. Yet even if the promised transformation takes longer than numbers surrounding AI companies imply, real economic benefits should stay - just as trains still ran after the Panic of 1873 that bankrupted railroad barons, while the internet didn't shut down after the 1990s dotcom bubble burst. "History is our friend in trying to understand this," said Coyle. "As long as one is left with the infrastructure that's needed to support all the productivity effects down the road, that's okay."

Source: Reuters

item.description:
Stephen Nellis
[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アップル、Ｍａｃのアクセス権限制御強化へ　ＡＩリスク対策 10/3 13:57 配信

3月にニューヨーク市で開催されたアップルのイベント　REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton

Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソフト（ＯＳ）を修正すると明らかにした。人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェントがＭａｃ内の全データへのアクセスを求めた場合に、利用者がより明確に認識し対応できるようにする。

メタ・プラットフォームズのＡＩエージェント「Ｍｕｓｅ」について、一部ユーザーから、機密性の高い個人情報にアクセスされたとの批判が出ている。

アップルのスマートフォン「ｉＰｈｏｎｅ」やタブレット端末「ｉＰａｄ」では、「サンドボックス化」と呼ばれる仕組みにより、初期設定ではどのアプリも別のアプリ内のデータにアクセスできない。一方、Ｍａｃはより柔軟な設計となっており、利用者の許可があれば、クラウドバックアップサービスなどのアプリが端末内の全データにアクセスできる「フルディスクアクセス」という設定がある。

アップルは２日、自社のサイトで、一部の開発者が利用者を危険にさらしかねない形でフルディスクアクセス機能を使っていると指摘し、今後、追加の制御機能を導入すると表明した。

「ＡＩエージェントの能力と自律性が高まるにつれ、これほど広範なアクセスに伴うリスクは大幅に増大する。利用者が自身のデータとプライバシーについて十分な情報に基づいて判断できるよう、アクセスを許可する前にこうしたリスクを明確に理解できるようにすることに取り組む」とした。

item.title: 米政権主要閣僚、イラン戦争やフーシ派巡り大統領山荘で協議 米報道
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - トランプ米政権の主要閣僚が２日、大統領山荘キャンプデービッドに集まり、イラン戦争、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの紛争への対応を協議した。米ニュースサイトのアクシオスが複数の米当局者の話として伝えた。

アクシオスによると、会合はバンス副大統領が主宰し、ルビオ国務長官、ヘグセス国防長官、ウィットコフ大統領特使、ラトクリフ中央情報局（ＣＩＡ）長官、ケイン統合参謀本部議長らが参加した。トランプ政権はこの会合について公表していないが、当局者の１人は「物事が決定された、あるいは少なくとも掘り下げた議論が行われた」と述べたという。

トランプ氏は２日午後、記者団からイランに対する次の一手について問われ、「それを話せば、大ニュースになるだろう」と述べ、「いずれ分かる。非常にうまく進んでいる。イランは厳しい状況だ」と語った。

中東や欧米当局者はロイターに、サウジがフーシ派に対する攻勢を計画していると述べた。紅海の海上輸送路の確保に向け沿岸部で攻勢をかける案や、複数の戦線で同時攻撃を仕掛ける案などが検討されており、向こう数週間以内に開始する可能性があるという。

item.title: ＯＰＥＣプラスの生産能力評価、11月中旬にずれ込みか 中東紛争が影響
item.description:
Alex Lawler Olesya Astakhova
［ロンドン／モスクワ ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Alex Lawler　Olesya Astakhova

［ロンドン／モスクワ　２日　ロイター］ - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）加盟国とロシアなど非加盟産油国で構成する「ＯＰＥＣプラス」で、加盟国の２０２７年の原油生産枠（クオータ）設定に向けた生産能力の評価作業が遅れていることが関係者の話で分かった。イラン戦争で中東の増産計画が混乱し、生産予測が不透明になっているという。

生産能力評価は２０２６年９月末までに完了する予定だったが、関係者によると、１１月中旬になる見通し。

ＯＰＥＣプラス加盟国の生産能力の試算は米石油コンサルタント会社のデゴルヤー・アンド・マクノートンが行っている。米国の制裁下にあるロシア、イラン、ベネズエラは対象外。

関係筋によると、同社のＯＰＥＣへの報告書提出は１１月半ばになる。この日程でも、ＯＰＥＣプラスは１１月下旬に開く次回の全体会合で評価結果を検討できる。

中東紛争により、一部加盟国で生産能力の拡大を予定していた事業に遅れが生じている。関係筋は、名指しを控えつつ、評価に必要なデータを提出していない国もあると述べた。

item.title: テニス＝ジョコビッチ、今季は「本当に苦しい」 体力でなく健康問題
item.description: ［北京 ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［北京　２日　ロイター］ - テニスの四大大会で２４回の優勝を誇るノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）が、２日の中国オープン（ＯＰ）で再びメディカルタイムアウトを必要とした後、今年は非常に苦しいシーズンを過ごしてきたと語った。原因はスタミナ不足ではなく、公表していない健康上の問題にあるという。

ジョコビッチはシングルス２回戦で、世界ランキング１０４位のブ・ユンチャオケテ（中国）と対戦し、４─６、７─６、６─２で逆転勝利。史上最多６回の優勝を果たしている中国ＯＰでの成績を３１勝０敗とした。

ジョコビッチは今年の全米ＯＰで、試合中に嘔吐したほか、背中や肩の不調にも悩まされた。終盤にはサーブにも影響が出て、２００６年の全豪ＯＰ以来となる四大大会初戦敗退に終わっていた。

１１年ぶりの出場となった今大会、１回戦でもメディカルタイムアウトを要求していたジョコビッチは、記者会見で自身の状態について、「詳細を話すつもりはない。そうすると、何かへの不満や言い訳を探しているように聞こえてしまうからだ。実のところ、今年はいくつかの問題に悩まされ、私にとって本当に厳しいシーズンとなっている」と語った。

「今年出場した試合や大会のほとんどは、フィジカル的に本当に、本当に苦しいものだった。それはスタミナの問題ではない。みんなはそこを混同しがちだが、スタミナではなく別の問題だ。健康面により関係していることだ」と述べた。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝フィリーズ、マッティングリー暫定監督が退任へ─報道
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のフィリーズが、ドン・マッティングリー暫定監督（６５）を退任させる方針だという。ＵＳＡトゥデーが２日に報じた。来週にも退任の見通しだが、球団は別の役職で残留する機会を提示するという。

フィリーズは今季レギュラーシーズンを８８勝７４敗で終え、１日に行われたブレーブスとのナ・リーグのワイルドカードシリーズ第３戦に２─６で敗戦。シリーズ敗退が決まった。

マッティングリー氏は１月、ロブ・トムソン前監督の下でベンチコーチとしてフィリーズに加入。ドジャースを２０１１─１５年、マーリンズを１６─２２年に率いた経験を持つマッティングリー氏はコーチ就任当時、監督への復帰に関心はないと話していたが、フィリーズが４月２８日に９勝１９敗の不振を受け、トムソン前監督を解任し、マッティングリー氏を暫定監督に昇格させた。

その後、チームは持ち直した。７月１８日時点で５５勝４４敗、マッティングリー氏就任後で４６勝２５敗を記録したが、７月末に失速。９月も１０勝１４敗にとどまり、最終的にナ・リーグ第３ワイルドカードでポストシーズンに進出した。

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 3 : Japan's government has begun recalibrating its messaging to reassure markets that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is not pursuing reflationary policies, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said in an interview with broadcaster TV Tokyo on Saturday. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent views Takaichi's economic policies as suited to current economic conditions, but has questioned whether the government has been communicating that message clearly enough to investors, Katayama said. "So we concluded around late August that we need to communicate that message more clearly to financial markets," Katayama said, addressing market perceptions that the administration's policies are reflationary.

item.title: サッカー＝マンＣ、プレミアリーグの財務規定巡る判断に不服申し立て
item.description: ［マンチェスター（英国） ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マンチェスター（英国）　２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグのマンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）は２日、同リーグの独立委員会から重大な財務規定違反が認定されたことを受け、不服申し立てを行ったと発表した。

プレミアリーグは９月２９日、マンＣが２００９年から１８年まで９シーズンにわたって商業パートナーとの「偽装契約」を締結し、収益を水増してコストを過少計上していたと独立委員会が認定したことを発表。９億ポンド（約１８８１億円）以上の操作を行い、財務規定を順守しているように装ったと認定した。

マンＣは多額の罰金や勝ち点剥奪、その他の競技上のペナルティーに加え、降格やタイトル剥奪の可能性も取りざたされている。

これまで不正行為を否定し続けてきたマンＣは声明で、１日の１９時に不服申し立てを行ったとし、「当クラブは、法解釈と原則、事実において、当該見解には明白かつ重大な誤りが複数含まれており、その判断が妥当性を欠くものであるという立場をとっている。当クラブはプレミアリーグによる告発について潔白であり、本件に関する当クラブの主張を裏付ける、反論の余地のない包括的な証拠が存在する」と述べた。

プレミアリーグの規定では、不服申し立てから１２週間以内に審理を行う。全面的な審理ではなく独立委員会の認定が正当か検討するもので、審理終了後３０日以内に決定を下す。

また、イングランド・サッカー協会（ＦＡ）は同日、財務規定違反が認定されてから初めてとなる公式声明で、「独立委員会の決定は、競技の公平性にとって重大な意味をもつ。われわれはその決定とそれが及ぼす影響を慎重に検討しており、適切な措置を講じる方針だ」と述べた。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝デューレン、5年約316億円でピストンズ残留へ─報道
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のピストンズが、制限付きフリーエージェント（ＦＡ）のセンター、ジェイレン・デューレン（２２）と５年総額２億ドル（約３１６億円）の契約を結ぶことが分かった。米ＥＳＰＮとジ・アスレチックが１日に報じた。契約は全額保証されるという。

両者は数カ月にわたり契約交渉を続けていたが、合意に至っていなかった。報道によると、ピストンズは昨季プレーオフでのデューレンのパフォーマンスなどを理由に、当初は低い条件を提示していた。直近では、デューレンに同じ総額２億ドルの契約を提示したものの、体重に関する条項を盛り込んでいたという。今回の合意では同条項が削除されたと報じられている。

昨季初めてオールスターとオールＮＢＡに選出されたデューレンは、レギュラーシーズンで自己最多の１試合平均１９．５得点に、１０．５リバウンドを記録。ピストンズは６０勝２２敗で東カンファレンス最高成績を残した。一方、プレーオフでは同１０．２得点、８．５リバウンドに数字を落とし、チームは東カンファレンス準決勝でキャバリアーズに３勝４敗で敗れた。

デューレンは２０２２年ドラフト１巡目全体１３位でＮＢＡ入りし、４シーズン全てをピストンズでプレー。通算では１試合平均１３．５得点、１０．３リバウンド、２．１アシストを記録している。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャース、スクバルがブレーブスとの第1戦で先発へ
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のドジャースは、３日に行われるブレーブスとのナ・リーグ地区シリーズ（ＮＬＤＳ）第１戦で左腕タリク・スクバル投手（２９）を先発起用することを決めた。

今季開幕投手を務め、昨季のプレーオフでも活躍した山本由伸投手ではなく、スクバルが第１戦を任される。スクバルは「第１戦に先発し、コーチ陣やチームメート、球団から信頼されてマウンドを託されるのは名誉であり、光栄なこと。チームを勝てる状況に持っていけるよう、自分にできることをしたい。楽しみにしている」と意気込みを示した。

ア・リーグのサイ・ヤング賞（最優秀投手賞）を２年連続で受賞しているスクバルは、８月２日にタイガースからトレードで加入。今季はタイガースで１６試合に先発して７勝５敗、防御率２．７９の数字を残し、ドジャース移籍後は１０試合で５勝２敗、防御率２．６１だった。

２０２０年にタイガースでメジャーデビューして以降、レギュラーシーズン通算では７シーズンで６６勝４４敗、防御率３．０２。タイガースで臨んだ過去２季のプレーオフでは６試合に先発して２勝１敗、防御率２．０４を記録し、チームは両年ともア・リーグ地区シリーズに進出した。

item.title: 9月雇用統計はトレンドに整合、次回会合までにさらなる情報＝クリーブランド連銀総裁
item.description:
Michael S. Derby
[２日 ロイター] - 米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁は２日、９月の米雇用...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
9月雇用統計はトレンドに整合、次回会合までにさらなる情報＝クリーブランド連銀総裁 10/3 10:19 配信

ニューヨーク市で2025年11月撮影　REUTERS/Brendan McDermid/File Photo

Michael S. Derby

[２日 ロイター] - 米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁は２日、９月の米雇用統計は最近の雇用情勢と整合的との認識を示した上で、今後の金融政策を決めるまでにはまだ時間があると述べた。

ハマック氏は米公共放送ＰＢＳの番組「ニュースアワー」のインタビューで、「過去１２カ月は平均で毎月４万１０００人の雇用が生まれている。これは私が推計する（雇用セクターの）ブレークイーブンとおおむね一致する」と述べ、労働市場が安定的に推移していることを示唆するとした。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金融政策対応については、「月末の会合までに、さらに多くの情報が得られる。２つの責務を確実に果たせるよう、適切な政策スタンスを決める時間は十分にある」と語った。

ＦＲＢは先月、約３年ぶりに０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定した。ハマック氏は、早い段階から利上げを支持してきた。

今週、複数のＦＲＢ高官が、追加利上げの前にデータを見極める時間があるとの認識を示した。また９月の雇用統計発表後、１０月２７─２８日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ観測が後退し、ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチでは据え置きの確率が８６％となっている。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：虚偽説明や失敗隠しも、中国系ＡＩエージェントにも「暴走」リスク アングル：欧米自動車メーカー、防衛需要取り込み推進　業績貢献は限定的か コラム：英バーナム首相、ＥＵ再接近に本腰　市場揺らす「ブリターン」構想 アングル：エヌビディア、ＡＩ半導体担保の巨大融資市場構想、資産価値巡りウォール街と溝 アングル：米株高支える高い増益、投資家は持続可能性に不安も 最終更新: 10/3(土) 10:19 ロイター

item.title: サッカー＝フランスはイタリアと引き分け、ジダン監督のホーム初陣
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）は２日、各地で１次リーグの試合を行い、リーグＡの１組ではフランスがホームでイタリアに１─１で引き分けた。

フランスは０─０で迎えた後半１０分、ゴール右寄りの位置でＦＫを得ると、少し動かしたボールをミカエル・オリーズが左足でシュートし、ネットを揺らした。しかし、同２３分に自陣でのボールロストからアレッサンドロ・バストーニに同点弾を許すと、同４０分にはダヨ・ウパメカノが２枚目のイエローカードを受けて退場した。

フランス指揮官就任後のホーム初戦をドローで終えたジネディーヌ・ジダン監督は、ＴＦ１で「選手たちのことを思うと非常に残念だ。われわれはもっと良い結果に値するプレーを見せていた。選手たちを誇りに思う。ハードワークやプレッシングは、まさに模範的だった」と振り返った。

同組のもう１試合では、ベルギーがホームでトルコと対戦。ケビン・デブルイネの２得点とロメル・ルカクのゴールにより、３─０で快勝した。

この結果、１組は３試合を終えて勝ち点７のフランスが首位。ベルギーは勝ち点６の２位で、イタリアは勝ち点４の３位。勝ち点０のトルコは最下位となっている。

item.title: Ｆ１＝バーレーンＧＰフリー走行、フェルスタッペンが最速
item.description: ［セパン（マレーシア） ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［セパン（マレーシア）　２日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１のバーレーン・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は２日、マレーシアのセパンでフリー走行を行い、レッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）がこの日のトップタイムを記録した。

中東情勢を受けてマレーシアで開催されている今大会、フェルスタッペンはフリー走行１回目に１分３７秒５２０をマークした。２回目でトップだったフェラーリのシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）が１分３７秒５２８で続き、その差はわずか０秒００８だった。

３番手は２回目に１分３７秒６２７を記録したレッドブルのアイザック・ハジャー（フランス）。昨季王者でマクラーレンのランド・ノリス（英国）が２回目に１分３７秒６６５で４番手だった。

個人総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（メルセデス、イタリア）は２回目の１分３８秒０６０が自己ベストで８番手だった。

item.title: サッカー＝久保建英選手が結婚、俳優の福原遥さんと
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部、レアル・ソシエダードに所属する日本代表ＭＦ久保建英選手が、俳優の福原遥さんと結婚したことを発表した。

両者は２日、それぞれのインスタグラムでツーショットの写真を披露し、「久保建英と福原遥は結婚致しましたことをご報告させていただきます。お互い、幼い頃からたくさんの方の支えがあって今があります。まだまだ未熟な私たちですが、皆様への感謝の気持ちを忘れることなく、共に助け合い、笑顔あふれる温かい家庭を築いていきたいと思っております」とコメントした。

２００１年生まれの久保選手は１１年にスペインの名門バルセロナの下部組織に加入。その後、ＦＣ東京で下部組織を経てトップチームデビューを飾るなどし、１９年にバルセロナの宿敵であるレアル・マドリードに移籍した。

スペインではマジョルカ、ビリャレアル、ヘタフェでもプレーした後、２２年に現在も所属するソシエダードに移籍。日本代表では１９年に１８歳でデビューを飾り、２２年と２６年のワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）に出場している。

item.title: Latvia PM Kulbergs wins election held under shadow of Ukraine war
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist, pro-Ukraine United List party won Saturday's parliamentary election by an unexpectedly wide margin, partial results showed, with many voters on edge amid warnings of potential Russian aggression.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas, Terje Solsvik
item.content:encoded: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist, pro-Ukraine United List party won Saturday's parliamentary election by an unexpectedly wide margin, partial results showed, with many voters on edge amid warnings of potential Russian aggression. With 88% of ballots counted, United List was on 36.6%, followed by the populist, MAGA-style Latvia First on 13.4%. Latvia First had courted the country's substantial ethnic Russian minority in the run-up to the vote. Baltic countries have warned for months that Russia is mounting sabotage, cyber and other hybrid attacks across Europe to erode support for Ukraine and sow fear, although Western officials dismiss concerns that Moscow is capable of launching a direct assault on NATO, of which Latvia is a member. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. Reacting to exit poll readings earlier in the evening, Kulbergs said he hoped to remain prime minister but that he would not want to govern with Latvia First. According to partial results, he will still need coalition allies to form a government. "It's remarkably good. I was not expecting such a result," Kulbergs said at his party's headquarters in Riga. Third in the exit poll ranking was the pro-Russian Sovereign Power party, on 11.6%, followed by the nationalist National Alliance, which promotes a hardline approach to the Kremlin, at 9.1%. SHADOW OF UKRAINE WAR A businessman and amateur rally driver, Kulbergs, 47, came to power in May after the previous coalition crumbled over its handling of incidents in which [USN:L1N41K03T TEXT:"stray military drones flew"] undetected into Latvia. Though the drones were Ukrainian, officials [USN:L8N41X1AC TEXT:"have blamed Russia"] for causing them to divert from their flight paths. "The priority, in my view, is, of course, security – security in Latvia," said Megija Nordena, 21, from Riga. "And then ... as a student, I’d say support for students, the economy, and also support for pensioners." Throughout his campaign, Kulbergs has also promised more anti-drone capabilities for Latvia and to maintain defence spending at 5% of gross domestic product, one of the highest levels in NATO. His pro-Kremlin rivals said Latvia should stop any aid to Ukraine and should instead focus more on cost-of-living issues, particularly among the country's Russian-speaking minority. "Our voters want peace, to stop looking for shelters, to no longer experience the air alerts," Sovereign Power party leader Julia Stepanenko told Reuters. "The war must not be encouraged in any way, including by financing it ... Ukraine must win, but through peace talks." The ethnic Russian minority in Latvia is split between those who feel embarrassed or angry about the Kremlin's war in Ukraine, and those frustrated with policies at home aimed at limiting their influence on public life that many see as discriminatory. Latvia, with a population of 1.9 million, is sandwiched between the Baltic Sea, and Russia and Belarus to the east, with EU and NATO allies Estonia and Lithuania to the north and south.

item.title: アジア大会＝サッカー日本女子代表、北朝鮮下し3連覇
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - 愛知・名古屋アジア大会は２日、サッカー女子決勝を行い、日本が北朝鮮との２─２からのＰＫ戦を５─３で制し、３大会連続最多４度目の優勝を果たした。

日本は前半３２分に上野真実が右足の鋭いシュートをゴール左に決めて先制。しかし、後半２分に追いつかれると、同２４分には逆転を許した。

それでも、同４１分に途中出場の西尾葉音が同点弾をマークし、延長戦へ。ＰＫ戦までもつれ込むと、北朝鮮の３人目のシュートをＧＫ大場朱羽がセーブ。日本は５人全員がＰＫを成功させた。

item.title: Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike on ventilator, attorneys say
item.description: The lawyers accused Correction Department officials of shrugging off prior warnings that pre-existing medical conditions would make placing IV lines especially difficult.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike on ventilator, attorneys say

The lawyers accused Correction Department officials of shrugging off prior warnings that pre-existing medical conditions would make placing IV lines especially difficult.

A picture taken on Dec 4, 2007, shows death-row inmate Christa Pike entering the Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tennessee, US, obtained by Reuters on Sep 30, 2026. (File photo: J. Miles Cary/ Knoxville News Sentinel/USA Today Network via Reuters)

03 Oct 2026 07:03AM (Updated: 03 Oct 2026 10:17AM)

FAST

NASHVILLE: Convicted killer Christa Pike was left gravely ill, unconscious and hospitalised on life support after Tennessee's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers said on Friday (Oct 2), providing the first detailed account of the injuries she suffered. Hospital staff were working to save Pike's life and clear the drug pentobarbital from her system, her attorneys said in an emergency motion, which seeks a court order for Tennessee's Department of Correction to preserve evidence from Wednesday night's botched execution. Pike remained in critical condition, intubated and hooked to a mechanical ventilator to breathe, her lawyers said, after two doses of pentobarbital were administered to her intravenously at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital. The bungled attempt to establish intravenous lines also left both her arms "swollen, burned and blistered", the apparent result of the pentobarbital, a highly alkaline and caustic substance, seeping into the tissues under her skin, the court filing said. 'VEINS HAD BLOWN'

The lawyers accused Correction Department officials of shrugging off prior warnings from Pike's doctors that pre-existing medical conditions — small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis — would make placing IV lines especially difficult. "At no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms. Pike's body," her lawyers said in a filing in the Chancery Court for Tennessee's 20th Judicial District. It said witnesses to the execution attempt could hear Pike "crying, whimpering and breathing loudly throughout the procedure". The filing provided the fullest picture yet of the medical consequences of an attempted execution that Tennessee Governor Bill Lee said followed the state's established protocol. It was the state's second botched execution this year, prompting Lee to halt any further attempts to carry out the death penalty for the rest of 2026. He also ordered an independent review of what went wrong.

Related:

Tennessee death row inmate in hospital after surviving two lethal injections

Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago of first-degree murder for her role in the torture and killing of a 19-year-old vocational school classmate, Colleen Slemmer, at the University of Tennessee campus in Knoxville in 1995, when Pike was 18. She had been scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries, and the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be executed in that state for a crime committed by a teenager. Pike's then-17-year-old boyfriend was tried as an adult and convicted of murder as well, but received a life sentence with eligibility for parole. A third schoolmate who was 18 at the time and acted as a lookout for the two others ended up testifying for the prosecution and received probation. Lee earlier this week rejected a clemency petition seeking to commute Pike's death penalty to a life prison term without the possibility of parole. The petition argued for leniency, in part, on the basis of her childhood history of severe neglect, sexual abuse that included two rapes, and untreated mental illness. The clemency petition also cited evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for her to control her impulses. The US Supreme Court on Wednesday lifted an 11th-hour stay of execution, which was issued earlier in the day by a federal appeals court to give more time to weigh Pike's claim that her childhood trauma was not properly considered in her sentencing. In their filing on Friday, Pike's lawyers urged the state Chancery Court to order preservation of evidence they said would show that state prison personnel violated her constitutional rights by subjecting her to cruel and unusual punishment.

Source: Reuters/bg

Apple says it will flag AI requests for Mac data after Meta's Muse draws complaints

Apple's new entry-level Mac laptop, the MacBook Neo is on display during an event in New York City, U.S., March 4, 2026. REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 2 : Apple said on Friday that it plans to change its Mac operating system to make it more obvious when AI agents ask to access all of the data on Macs. Some users have criticized Meta's Muse, an AI agent capable of carrying out complex tasks like canceling unused subscriptions or haggling for better prices. These people claimed the agent accessed what users believed to be private messages. On Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another app by default, a technique called sandboxing. But Apple's Macs are more flexible, with a "Full Disk Access" option that allows apps such as cloud backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission. Apple on Friday said some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.

"Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action," Apple wrote in a post. "As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy." Apple's move comes after Inc magazine technology columnist Jason Aten accused Meta's Muse of reading private messages on his Mac. He said he had not enabled Full Disk Access. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone pushed back against those claims last week, saying Muse's access to Apple's Messages app is strictly opt-in.  "You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content," Stone wrote on social media platform X. "It can't read your Messages unless you do this. And it can be revoked at any time." Apple declined to comment beyond its post. Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 北朝鮮が弾道ミサイル、日本ＥＥＺ外に落下 韓国は追加発射を警戒
item.description: ［ソウル／東京 ３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ソウル／東京　３日　ロイター］ - 日韓の防衛当局は３日、北朝鮮が東岸沖へ弾道ミサイルを発射したと発表した。日本の防衛省は、日本の排他的経済水域（ＥＥＺ）外へ落下したと推定している。北朝鮮が弾道ミサイルを発射するのは９月２０日以来。

韓国は国家安全保障会議を招集。同国軍は追加の発射に警戒を強めている。

韓国軍の合同参謀本部によると、北朝鮮は午前６時３０分ごろに東部の元山付近から弾道ミサイルを発射した。日本の防衛省は飛行距離６８０キロ程度、最高高度９０キロ程度と分析。韓国軍は７００キロ以上飛行したと分析している。日本政府は北朝鮮に厳重に抗議した。

韓国と北朝鮮は、非武装地帯（ＤＭＺ）で発生した地雷の爆発を巡って非難の応酬を続けている。韓国は、北朝鮮の地雷で自国の兵士が重傷を負ったと主張。北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の妹、金与正党総務部長は２日、韓国側の非難を「根拠がない」として一蹴し、韓国側の謝罪要求も退けた。

item.title: G7 nations will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel after prices soar
item.description: The Group of Seven wealthy democracies said Friday that they plan to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products in the coming weeks, starting with “substantial” amounts of diesel after the ...
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: WASHINGTON — The Group of Seven wealthy democracies said Friday that they plan to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products in the coming weeks, starting with “substantial” amounts of diesel after the fuel recently hit record high prices in the United States. U.S. President Donald Trump said the diesel release would happen “immediately,” echoing a G7 promise to start “immediately” with a “frontloaded substantial release” of diesel within the next 20 days and the rest over four months. Trump and his Republican Party face pressure to address surging prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, and Trump announced the action Friday on social media. The president’s approval ratings on the economy hit a new low, according to an AP-NORC poll, as the Iran war and his trade battles have increased U.S. prices for oil and other goods. Gas prices in the U.S. and abroad have soared during the eight-month-long war, a cost Trump has repeatedly said is worth it for making sure Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons. The national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. was US$6.37 on Friday, according to AAA, after hitting a record US$6.52 on Sept. 22. Diesel prices have hit records in Europe, too. The release of diesel in Europe might mean less exports of diesel from the U.S., which could lower prices by 25-50 cents per gallon after a few weeks, said Michael Lynch, distinguished fellow at Energy Policy Research Foundation, a non-partisan research institution focused on energy and economics. Macron says the decision should bring down prices France holds the rotating presidency of the G7 group and made the announcement in a statement released after videoconference talks that Macron presided over. The G7 countries are Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the U.K. and the U.S., plus EU representation. The release follows on from a March announcement that International Energy Agency member countries would release 426 million barrels of oil and products to stabilize the oil market. European Union countries committed about 92 million barrels, a promise weighted toward refined products made from crude such as diesel. “This common decision and this unity should bring down prices,” Macron said. “The volumes we’re releasing should also add liquidity to the market and bring down prices.” In addition to the rise in the price of the crude oil from which diesel is made, other factors include the decision by Russia to ban exports due to Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries. Europe does not import Russian diesel, but other buyers of Russian diesel such as Turkey and Latin American countries must now compete with Europe for available barrels. Meanwhile refined product shipments from the Persian Gulf producers have fallen due to war damage and blocked export routes. The statement pushed U.S. oil prices down two per cent but “the impact was lessened by lack of clarity on an important question,” said Pavel Molchanov, investment strategy analyst at Raymond James. Is the 100 million barrels in addition to the amount already agreed in March, or “is this the final portion of the existing pledge?” he said. The G7 says export bans are off the table Some Republicans in the U.S. had called for Trump to ban U.S. exports of diesel to try to bring domestic prices down. But the G7 statement said the group agreed not to limit energy exports to each other. Oil market analysts warn a U.S. export ban could lower prices in the short term but eventually backfire by reducing supplies of gasoline since diesel output can’t be lowered without also cutting overall refinery production. Asked about a potential U.S. export ban on Friday, Trump said “we were never going to do it.” “We’re not going to be doing the export ban,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “We’re going to be doing what we’re supposed to do.” He added that Europe is making “a major world contribution, and so are we.” Experts say there are risks in the strategy The emergency release could also be a short-term fix with the potential to do long-term harm, said Jim Krane, energy research fellow at Rice University’s Baker Institute. “Draining stocks will reduce retail fuel prices for a while, at the cost of leaving Europe with less emergency cover,” Krane said. “At some point in the future Europe and the rest of the G7 will have to refill their strategic reserves. Normally they try to do this when prices are low. Nobody knows when that will happen. It’s a risk.” With two wars raging that involve attacks on refineries and exports, “it’s not the best time to be frittering away your emergency stocks -- especially when there is no visibility on future prices or peace agreements,” Krane said. Trump had a conversation overnight with Macron about the need to address rising fuel prices and the availability of petroleum products, according to the French Embassy in the U.S. Macron on Friday then chaired the videoconference of G7 leaders to discuss the issue. Besides his call with Macron, Trump on Friday called in to the meeting with the G7 leaders to negotiate the release of the European diesel stockpiles, according to a White House official who was not authorized to speak publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity. Trump on Thursday embarked on what he said would be a 32-day marathon of rallies to try to bolster his party’s chances for keeping control of the U.S. House and Senate in the November elections. The president has grown increasingly frustrated with what he sees as a disconnect between his achievements and the public’s view of his work. This week he gave himself an A-plus for his work on the economy but said “we’re doing an extremely poor job of promotion.” Collin Binkley and John Leicester, The Associated Press Leicester reported from Paris. AP writer Michelle L. Price contributed to this report. AP Business Writer David McHugh contributed from Frankfurt, Germany and Cathy Bussewitz contributed from New York.
